note: status is one of open|fixed|not-a-defect. The gate requires every blocker and major to be fixed or not-a-defect, each with a resolution naming its evidence.

findings.what: All 33 field-entry marker triangles are painted as three thin hairline rules forming an open grey "F"/"⊨" instead of the official's solid black right-pointing triangle.
findings.where: Every field marker on the sheet, e.g. DLN at ~(19.2, 34.7)-(23.2, 38.7) pt; also TIN at (32.6, 196.2), RDO at (200.2, 197.0), item 17 at (189.2, 440.8). 33 instances page-wide.
findings.evidence: Seen side by side at 4x and 7x: official prints a filled black ► ; ours prints a light-grey open F. Source PDF draws ONE filled path (type 'f', fill (0,0,0)) with segments (19.16,34.72)->(23.16,36.72)->(19.16,38.72)->(19.16,34.72). The emitted SVG at that spot has three axis-aligned rects instead: h0 x=19.16 y=34.6 w=4 h=0.24, v192 x=19.04 y=34.72 w=0.24 h=4, h3 x=19.16 y=36.6 w=4 h=0.24. The two diagonal edges were flattened to horizontals and the fill dropped. A PDF scan counts 33 filled-triangle drawings on this page and 0 on every other page in my batch.
findings.resolution: emit.py renders page["paths"]: the 33 markers are single closed <path> elements on the source's own points, fill #000000 (`M32.88 27.6L36.96 29.52L32.88 31.44L32.88 27.6Z` for the first). 0605 page 1 emits 52 paths of which 43 are black-filled - 33 markers plus the 10 decimal points of F002 - and a 110dpi print-to-PDF crop shows solid black triangles at DLN, PSIC and every field marker. Measured on a scratch regeneration of all 51 forms from the post-Round-1 IR: rules 100% on 51/51 with rules_missing 0 and rules_extra 0, paper exact 51/51, text 100% on 51/51 with text_missing 0 and text_extra 0.

findings.what: The pre-printed decimal point is missing from all 10 money boxes; it is dropped at the extract stage and never reaches the IR or the SVG.
findings.evidence: At 4x the official shows a clear black dot near the right edge of items 19, 20D and 21; our boxes are empty. Source PDF has filled shapes (type 'fs', fill (0,0,0)) ~1.68 x 1.5 pt at those coordinates. IR page 1 has no rule and no area_fill anywhere in x 548-562 / y 465-530, and a regex scan of the emitted SVG returns 0 elements in that box. Note every other form in my batch (0619-E, 0619-F, 0620, 1600-PT, 1600-VT) does render its decimal marks, so 0605 is the outlier.
findings.resolution: Same emit.py change: the decimal points are filled Bezier circles, four `c` ops each, and are now emitted as <path> with their control points intact. Exactly 10 curve paths land in the money column of page 1. Measured on a scratch regeneration of all 51 forms from the post-Round-1 IR: rules 100% on 51/51 with rules_missing 0 and rules_extra 0, paper exact 51/51, text 100% on 51/51 with text_missing 0 and text_extra 0.

findings.what: Four short hairline dashes that the official paints just above the ATC table's top border are missing; same extract-stage drop as the missing decimal points.
findings.evidence: Column-darkness profile over x 130-165 pt: at scanline y=46.12 pt the official has 20 dark pixels, ours has 0; both are identical from y=46.50 down (94 px, the black border). findings.what: After the ATC table was relocated to guide.html, its grey header band and its full-height left/right border rules were left behind, drawing a large empty framed box down two-thirds of the filed page.
findings.evidence: In the HTML page 2 I see an empty grey strip under "Total Taxes Withheld and Remitted" and two long vertical rules running to y~746 pt with nothing between them; the official has the full Table 1 ATC table there. Confirmed in the emitted SVG: two #d9d9d9 rects at the cut line plus the two 461.33pt-tall black rules. provenance.json records cut_y_pt 286.02 and "straddlers_kept_by_form": 5.
findings.resolution: Re-measured on the current bundle. forms/1600-pt-2018/provenance.json now records cut_y_pt 283.91 with straddlers_kept_by_form 0 (the finding cited 286.02 and 5). Nothing is emitted below that cut: in forms/1600-pt-2018/index.html the page-2 rule SVG's lowest painted edge is y=283.37pt, 0 of its 148 rects fall below the cut, no cell extends past y1=283.91 and the lowest page-2 text div sits at top=270.0. The two #d9d9d9 rects at (29.5,286.0)/(34.2,286.0) and the 461.33pt rules v85 and v148 (y 284.45-745.78), still present in build/ir/1600-pt-2018.ir.json, are dropped by the emitter. build/audit.json for 1600-pt-2018 reports rules_below_guide_cut holds with area_fills_below_cut 0, and the relocated Table 1 ATC content is in guide.html (the string 'Table 1' occurs in guide.html and not in index.html).

findings.what: White (invisible) BIR internal reviewer initials from the source page are rendered as visible black rows appended to "Table 1 - Alphanumeric Tax Code (ATC)" in guide.html, so hidden content is published and reads as ATC data.
findings.where: guide.html, last 6 rows of the ATC table. Source PDF page 2 at (28.8, 776.97) through (305.81, 859.27) pt.
findings.evidence: Read the rendered guide: six trailing rows "MMC ___ AAE ___ MCZ ___ AES ___", "MLIB ___ ECHR ___ YVL ___ RRGM ___", "MTMI ___ RCC ___ TBV ___", "LCB ___ MTM ___ JHB ___", "NAC ___ RSDV ___ WPM ___", "RPRR ___ JBA ___ GPS ___" sitting inside the ATC table in black. In the source PDF these spans carry color 16777215 (0xFFFFFF, white on white paper) at 12pt Times New Roman - invisible in the official. The IR keeps 25 such white runs on page 2 and the guide emitter paints them black.
findings.resolution: emit.py carries each run's colour into the reflowed guide: _line_pieces() keeps (text, colour) per run and _render_pieces() emits a span only where the colour is not black. The six rows of BIR reviewer initials are now `<span style="color:#ffffff">MMC ______ AAE _____ ...` - invisible on paper, exactly as in the official - and white runs are still present in the document rather than filtered out.

Confirmed structurally: 4 rows match empty first cell plus a percent rate.
findings.resolution: emit.py reflows the relocated table on lattice.py's own rows and columns instead of one row per printed line. 1600-PT's guide table is now 30 rows of NATURE OF PAYMENT | TAX RATE | ATC with every rate on its description's row: the two-line 'Franchise Tax on radio & TV broadcasting companies...' row carries '3%' and 'WB 050'. Stranded rate-only rows on this page: 3 -> 0, measured by rebuilding the region through the old and the new path.

findings.what: In the guide document the source title is broken mid-sentence and its trailing fragment is promoted to a heading: "BIR FORM No. 1600 WP – Remittance Return of Percentage Tax on Winnings and Prizes Withheld" is a paragraph, then "by Race Track Operators" is rendered as a standalone bold heading.

findings.what: Guide document emits raw Wingdings Private Use Area characters, so every bullet renders as an empty tofu box instead of the official's round and square bullets.
findings.where: forms/1601-fq-2020/guide.html — "Required Attachments:" list (2 bullets) and the "Note: All background information..." list (2 bullets). Four occurrences total.
findings.evidence: Screenshotted the .gl-page element and read the lower third; all four list markers render as hollow squares. Rendered page 1 of '1601-FQ Sep 2020 Guide.pdf' with fitz (clip 300,600-612,780 at 3x) and looked at it: the official uses a round bullet '•' for Required Attachments and a small filled square '▪' for the Note items. Grepping the emitted HTML for PUA code points: 1601-fq-2020/guide.html contains 0xF0B7 x2 and 0xF0A7 x2. The same defect is in every guide I have: 1601c-2018 0xF0A7 x2, 1601eq-2019 0xF0A7 x3, 1602q-2019 0xF0A7 x2, 1603q-2018 0xF0A7 x2. guide.css declares no font-family, so nothing in the stack carries these glyphs. A hollow square next to "The last 5 digits of the 14-digit TIN..." also reads as an unticked checkbox, which the official bullet does not.

findings.what: Guide reflow merges two separate bulleted items into one running paragraph and splits one line into two, and drops the bold on a heading.
findings.where: forms/1601-fq-2020/guide.html, "Note: All background information must be properly filled out." section, and the "b.3 Mandatory Continuing Legal Education (MCLE) Compliance Number; and" line just below it.
findings.evidence: Read the guide screenshot next to the fitz render of the official guide PDF. Official: "Note: All background information must be properly filled out." is bold, and the two square-bullet items ("The last 5 digits..." / "All returns filed by an accredited tax agent...") are on separate lines. Ours: the Note heading is regular weight, and the two bullets run together as one paragraph reading "[box] The last 5 digits of the 14-digit TIN refers to the branch code [box] All returns filed by an accredited tax agent on behalf of a taxpayer shall bear the following information:". Separately, "b.3 Mandatory Continuing Legal Education (MCLE)" and "Compliance Number; and" are emitted as two paragraphs where the official has one line.

findings.what: Interior word positions inside a text run drift up to 7.2pt out of alignment because the emitter reproduces a run's total width with one uniform letter-spacing value instead of the source's per-character origins.
findings.where: Page 1, item 9 "Registered Address" italic parenthetical. Run starts at x 110.9 pt, y 186.0 pt and ends near x 590 pt. Maximum interior displacement 7.16 pt, worst around the middle of the line (roughly x 250-420 pt).
findings.evidence: Looked at 8x side-by-side crops of y 183-194pt in two halves (x 105-360 and x 340-600). In the official there is a wide gap after "complete address." and the rest of the line is set tight; in ours the gap is a single normal space and the whole line is tracked looser, so every word from "If branch," onward sits progressively to the right of the official — most visibly around "indicate the branch address". Both lines start and end at the same x (the second crop shows "...by using BIR Form No. 1905)" landing identically), which is exactly why the geometric differ scores text_pct 100.0. Went to the data: forms/1601c-2018/index.html emits the run as a single div with letter-spacing:0.0668pt applied uniformly (same pattern on the equivalent 1602Q run), while build/ir/<slug>.ir.json records true per-character positions in char_origin_offsets_pt. Computing max|uniform-model - true origin| per run over all six forms: 1601-fq-2020 10/355 runs >0.5pt, 1601c-2018 47/293, 1601eq-2019 3/472, 1602q-2019 64/520, 1603q-2018 41/299, 1604c-2018 3/108. The 7.16pt item-9 case is present on page 1 of ALL SIX forms (1604-C's variant is 7.27pt at x 125.4, y 207.1).

findings.what: Same uniform-letter-spacing defect, visible as numbered Schedule 4 labels whose text sits ~1.2pt left of the official because a single large kern after the item number is smeared across the whole label.
findings.where: Page 2, Schedule 4 "Summary of Interest/Yield Paid and Accrued for the Month", left column. Run '1. On Deposit Liabilities' at x 21.6 pt, y 756.8 pt; run '2. On Bills Payables/Borrowed Funds' at x 21.6 pt, y 782.4 pt.
findings.evidence: Spotted by eye in the y 690-936pt band comparison, then confirmed on a 9x side-by-side crop of x 18-160pt / y 754-792pt: the official clearly shows "1.  On Deposit Liabilities" with a wide gap after the period, ours shows "1. On Deposit Liabilities" with a single space, and every following letter is shifted left. Went to the data: fitz rawdict per-character origins in the source PDF give the space ending at x=29.41 but 'O' starting at x=30.60, i.e. a 1.19pt explicit TJ kern. The IR run text is '1. On Deposit Liabilities ' (single space) and the emitted HTML applies that 1.19pt as letter-spacing spread over ~18 characters. Adjacent runs 'Taxable' and 'Exempt' are separate absolutely-positioned runs and align perfectly, which makes the misalignment of the numbered lines more conspicuous.

findings.what: Eight degenerate 0.6pt-wide field inputs are generated hard against the form's right outer border — invisible, unusable, but focusable in the tab order.
findings.where: Page 3, all at x 594.6 pt (the form box's right edge is at ~595.2 pt), y 44.4, 111.6, 131.2, 156.7, 164.8, 172.7, 188.6 and 196.7 pt; heights 6.6 to 66.3 pt. Element ids p3c3-i, p3c8-i, p3c11-i, p3c40-i, p3c55-i, p3c70-i, p3c97-i, p3c112-i.
findings.evidence: Enumerated every input/textarea/select in the browser for all six forms and measured its client rect against the .page rect. 1602Q page 3 is the only place with sub-2pt-wide inputs (8 of 1331). Their x is 594.6pt, i.e. the sliver between the Schedule 5/6 table's right rule and the outer border on the page whose lower 71% was relocated to guide.html. Everything else was clean across the batch: 0 inputs overlapping pre-printed .t text by >50% of the text's area, 0 inputs outside their page box, and 0 inputs with a visible border or non-transparent background, on all six forms (818/897/774/1331/609/294 inputs respectively).

findings.what: A solid opaque black rectangle is painted over the header, completely obliterating the pre-printed "BCS/" and "Item:" field labels, because the image's SMask (alpha channel) was dropped during extraction.
findings.where: Page 1 header, top-left, immediately right of the "For BIR Use Only" grey box. Black rect spans x 63.00-106.32 pt, y 31.08-48.48 pt (43.3 x 17.4 pt). It covers text runs 'BCS/ ' (x 63.62-84.58, y 31.12-40.09) and 'Item: ' (x 63.62-88.06, y 40.24-49.21).
findings.evidence: Screenshotted forms/1604c-2018/index.html at DPR 2 and rendered page 1 of '1604-C Jan 2018 Final.pdf' with fitz at the same pixel size, then looked at a 10x side-by-side crop of x 18-130pt / y 25-54pt. Ours shows a filled black block; the official shows the words "BCS/" and "Item:" on white. Went to the data: build/ir/1604c-2018.ir.json page 1 has NO area_fill and NO rule in that region, but image xref 45 (name Image45) at exactly x0=63.0 y0=31.08 x1=106.32 y1=48.48. In the source PDF that XObject is '/Width 120 /Height 48 /ColorSpace /DeviceRGB /SMask 46 0 R' and its base RGB is uniform black (39 bytes Flate). Reading SMask xref 46 with fitz gives alpha min=0, max=0, mean=0.0, pct_opaque=0.0 — i.e. the image is 100% transparent in the official. The emitted asset forms/assets/57521bfe...png is RGBA 120x48 with exactly ONE unique colour [0,0,0,255], alpha mean 255.0: the alpha channel was replaced by fully opaque. Not a rasteriser artifact — the pixels are opaque black in the asset file itself. audit.json scores this form rules_pct 100.0, text_pct 100.0, images_missing 0, images_placement_violations 0, because the image payload hash and placement rect are both correct; only the alpha is wrong.
findings.resolution: Stale evidence predating SMask compositing. The asset for source xref 39/SMask 40 (57521bfe...png, 120x48) now decodes with all 5,760 pixels at alpha 0: the placement paints nothing, and the pre-printed 'BCS/' and 'Item:' text runs it used to obliterate are emitted as text and visible. Verified by decoding the shipped asset and compositing over white (blank) on 2026-08-06.

findings.what: The same dropped-SMask bug paints a black bar along the top edge and a black column down the right edge of the "For BIR / Use Only" grey box, where the official has nothing and a thin hairline divider.
findings.where: Page 1 header, top-left. Image43 occupies x 23.52-69.00 pt, y 28.56-49.08 pt; the spurious black is a ~2.5pt strip along its top (y 28.6-31.1) and a ~4pt column at its right (x ~64-69) that merges into the Image45 block.
findings.evidence: Same 10x side-by-side crop as above. In ours the grey "For BIR / Use Only" panel is capped by a heavy black bar on top and bounded by a black column on the right; in the official the panel is a plain grey rectangle with a thin black vertical rule separating it from "BCS/". Source PDF xref 43 is '/SMask 44 0 R'; reading SMask 44 gives alpha min=0, max=255, mean=200.6, pct_opaque=78.7 — about a fifth of the image is meant to be transparent. The emitted asset forms/assets/b391a155...png is RGBA with colours [[0,0,0,255],[217,217,217,255]] and alpha mean 255.0, so the transparent 21% is being painted as opaque black instead. For contrast, 1601-fq-2020's two SMask'd images (p1 xref 44, p2 xref 49) have alpha mean 255.0 / pct_opaque 100.0, which is why dropping the SMask is harmless there and that form looks correct — 1604-C is the only one of my six where it bites.
findings.resolution: Stale evidence predating SMask compositing. Asset b391a155...png now decodes 5,550 opaque grey pixels with 1,506 transparent pixels forming exactly the top strip and right column the finding measured as spurious black; composited over white and inspected visually 2026-08-06 it is the official's plain grey 'For BIR Use Only' panel, no black bar or column.

findings.what: A solid opaque black rectangle is painted over the top-left of the sheet, completely obliterating the pre-printed "BCS/ Item:" label that the official form prints there.
findings.where: Page 1 header, x 63.0-106.3pt, y 31.1-48.5pt (immediately right of the "For BIR Use Only" grey box)
findings.evidence: I rendered both at 2x and compared: the official PDF shows white paper with the words "BCS/" and "Item:"; our page shows a filled black block. Root cause traced in the source: PDF xref 39 is a 120x48 DeviceRGB image with /SMask 40 (alpha), and its base RGB stream is only 39 compressed bytes (a flat black fill). The IR records sha256 57521bfe6748c51cf1a552d0868198a3bddf388f4de3c098f60cf02e6954f77b for that image, which is byte-identical to the PDF base image WITHOUT the SMask - the alpha channel was dropped, so the transparent stencil became an opaque rectangle. A second SMask'd image (xref 37 / SMask 38) sits at x 23.5-69.0, y 28.6-49.1 and shows the same black bleed along its top edge. The text div for "BCS/" still exists at left:63.62pt top:30.75pt - it is simply buried under the SVG <image> (elementsFromPoint at 85pt,40pt returns the SVG image, then svg z-index:1, then the page div). Audit reports images_missing 0, images_placement_violations 0, text 100%.
findings.resolution: Same stale dropped-SMask evidence as F020, same asset: 57521bfe...png decodes with all 5,760 pixels fully transparent, so nothing is painted over the 'BCS/ Item:' labels. Verified by decode + white-composite visual look 2026-08-06.

findings.what: In the guide document, the Wingdings bullet character renders as an empty missing-glyph box (tofu) instead of a filled square bullet.
findings.where: guide.html, the NOTE list under "Signature Lines" ("The last 5 digits of the 14-digit TIN..." and "All returns filed by an accredited tax agent..."). Source origin: 1604F p2 Wingdings spans at (332.59,701.36) and (332.59,709.40)pt.
findings.evidence: SAW two hollow boxes where the official prints filled square bullets. The guide emits the raw Private Use Area codepoint U+F0A7 (x2), which only means a bullet in Wingdings; guide.css loads no @font-face at all and sets the text in Georgia/Times, so the browser has no glyph for it. Measured at r20 on the tree that was written, by a checker that reads the SOURCE-derived offender box out of the r19 audit and the inputs out of the shipped index.html, and never consults the r20 audit -- so a box that cleared because its row PEER lost an input would still read as uncovered. Corpus input count went UP by 60; nothing was deleted. Cause: two producer bugs in lattice.py -- `GroupGeometry.span` excluded a cluster's own defining rule from its coverage, and `assign_points` placed a text run by its bounding-box centre (the run's ADVANCE), so the whitespace between "Calendar" and "Fiscal" counted as printed text inside the checkbox drawn in that gap. `glyph_ink_spans` now reads the per-character origins the IR already carries.

findings.resolution: The Fiscal box at (106.08, 123.12)-(119.52, 135.00) -> cell p1c7, 1 input (HEAD: p1c9 `label`, 0). Measured at r20 on the tree that was written, by a checker that reads the SOURCE-derived offender box out of the r19 audit and the inputs out of the shipped index.html, and never consults the r20 audit -- so a box that cleared because its row PEER lost an input would still read as uncovered. The assertion that owns this population, `printed_box_peers_all_fillable`, goes 14 offenders on 14 of 53 forms -> 0 on 0, and audit.py is byte-identical (sha256 8d22a957...), so nothing about the check moved. Corpus input count went UP by 60; nothing was deleted. Cause: two producer bugs in lattice.py -- `GroupGeometry.span` excluded a cluster's own defining rule from its coverage, and `assign_points` placed a text run by its bounding-box centre (the run's ADVANCE), so the whitespace between "Calendar" and "Fiscal" counted as printed text inside the checkbox drawn in that gap. `glyph_ink_spans` now reads the per-character origins the IR already carries.

findings.what: In the guide, a superscript text run is reordered out of "(4th)", corrupting two sentences: a paragraph ends "...is imposed upon th)" and the next begins "...beginning the fourth (4 taxable year".
findings.where: forms/1702q-2018/guide.html, section "Minimum Corporate Income Tax (MCIT)" (relocated from form page 3)
findings.evidence:
Read the rendered guide and then the HTML source:

A minimum corporate income tax (MCIT) of two percent (2%) of the gross income is imposed upon th)

any domestic corporation and resident foreign corporation beginning the fourth (4 taxable year (whether calendar...

. The source PDF page 3 text reads "...is imposed upon any domestic corporation and resident foreign corporation beginning the fourth (4th) taxable year (whether calendar or fiscal year..." — one sentence, no break.
findings.resolution: FIXED in r39 in emit._group_lines. The three runs sit at baseline 456.43 and the superscript 'th) ' at 454.39 -- 2.04pt away, 0.04pt OUTSIDE the 2.00pt LINE_BASELINE_TOLERANCE_PT, so it became a line of its own and reading order published '...is imposed upon th)' / '...the fourth (4 taxable year'. THE WINDOW WAS NOT WIDENED. _is_set_fragment proves two runs are one printed line by ink instead: one band strictly inside the other -- which two runs of the same size on different baselines can never satisfy, so it can never merge two ordinary lines -- and abutting within the word-space gap _line_pieces already uses. The corpus is not close on it: all 32 stranded fragments abut within [-0.12, +0.31]pt, while 2553's 9.33pt 'BIR Form No.' genuinely inside its 20.85pt title overlaps by -4.60pt and is refused. 29 merges on 9 pages, 27 of them ordinal superscripts, every one independently flagged superscript:True by MuPDF -- a flag the geometric rule never consulted. Three guides improve and no others: 1702Q reads 'the fourth (4th) taxable year'; 1701MS stops publishing two stranded superscripts as <h3> HEADINGS; 2000-DST's ATC cells read '1st P 2,000' instead of 'st 1 P 2,000'. Three scratch-copy mutants each trip exactly one of the three new assertions.

findings.what: Item 8A 'If yes, please specify' — the comb band is drawn but has no input, so the answer cannot be entered.
findings.evidence: DOM query x 30-600 / y 320-372 returns only six checkbox inputs (items 8 Yes/No and item 9's four boxes); nothing in the 8A band. Filled screenshot shows the comb ticks with no digits. Layout cell p1c51 (x 17.64-594.48, y 318.17-347.33) is kind='mixed', with no field cell carved out for the answer.
findings.resolution: DIAGNOSED in r39, not fixed, and NOT the P1 knockout-bite mechanism. The comb is registered and then SUPPRESSED: layout subject p1@17.64,318.17,594.48,347.33, state retained_unresolved, emission suppressed, reason_codes [emission-suppressed-no-rectangular-owner, painted-edge-partition], blocks_gate true, legacy_comb 25 cells / 24 dividers / pitch 14.40. The source agrees it is a comb: 24 printed dividers of 0.24pt at x 248.09->579.34 in steps of 14.40, between rails at 233.57 and 593.76, over y 339.65-347.09 = 25 compartments. It has no rectangular owner because the cell walk cuts the band at y=343.44 -- a lattice line induced by the Yes/No checkbox bottom edges h68 (x 190.80-203.16) and h69 (x 132.96-145.32), BOTH ENTIRELY LEFT of the comb's left rail at 233.57. There is no ink at all in x 233.7-594.5 at y 343.2-344.5, yet the walk cuts there, leaving eight 3.89pt blank strips matching neither the compartments nor the band. Zero inputs in x 233-595, y 339-348 in the shipped bytes. The fix is to bound a lattice line by the x-extent of the ink that induces it, or to let a comb band own a partition it spans -- the F196/F201 family, corpus-wide blast radius, and the user's call.

findings.what: Item 9 'Others (please specify)' — the white specify line is drawn but has no input.
findings.evidence: Same DOM query returns no input in that x range; the filled screenshot shows the white line empty while the four checkboxes on the row fill. Layout cell p1c55 spanning the row is kind='label'.
findings.resolution: DIAGNOSED in r39, not fixed, TWO independent barriers and both are deliberate. (1) The line is run p1t78, '(please specify) ____...', x 430.15-583.49, in UNEMBEDDED Arial Narrow -- the single ruled-blank refusal in the whole corpus (119 groups seen, 118 published, 1 refused with reason 'no single face states this glyph's outline'). substitutable_faces correctly yields no face: MuPDF's own name cleaner does not resolve 'Arial Narrow' to a base-14 alias, and the module refuses both a hand-written table and a machine-installed font. That refusal is right and must not be weakened to close this. (2) Even with a face, F200's own measurement says 117 of 118 published blanks yield no writing surface, and the strip below this bar would be a ~4pt sliver. The real writing area is the white knockout the sheet paints at x 471.82-583.66, y 351.53-360.89 ON THE GREY BAND, which has no rules around it, so nothing turns it into a field today. Making a rule-less knockout on a tone band a writing surface is a new relation with corpus-wide reach. Item 9's four checkboxes (p1c56-p1c59) ARE fillable; only the specify text cannot be entered. MEASURED AGAIN in W1 (F206): the knockout band emit.knockout_specify_band computes for this cell is (471.82, 351.53, 583.66, 360.89) -- exactly this finding's own coordinates -- confirming the knockout and its decorative tint are real and meaningful. But the caption run carrying "(please specify)" also carries the unresolved underscore sequence this finding already refuses to turn into a rule, and W1's ink-blocking test excludes a cell's own runs by their WHOLE bounding box (not per glyph, which is what keeps captions like 2553's ATC codes correctly out of the marker), so that run's box covers virtually the entire knockout and no candidate band survives. W1's own mechanism, run directly against this cell with its caption gate satisfied, confirms: no band. This finding's diagnosis and both its barriers stand exactly as written.

findings.resolution: FIXED in r39, upstream in extract.py, and the root cause is shared with F102. extract_text_runs published one run per MuPDF rawdict SPAN, and a span can carry two baselines: the source sets a lone space at (66.26, 113.78) and 'Calendar' at (75.50, 117.50) as separate text operators, and the merged span published the SPACE's baseline for the word. extract.baseline_groups now cuts a span at every baseline change -- faithful, not a repair, since the source drew each stretch with its own Td. Verified by the operator in the shipped IR: 'Calendar' is now baseline 117.50, x 75.50-114.48, y 109.36-119.39, identical to 'Fiscal' at 117.50 and beside 'For' at 117.26 -- and exactly the review's own measurement of the official (x 75-114, y 109.4-119.4). Census first: only 24 of 19,333 ink-bearing spans carried two baselines, and span bbox equalled the union of char bboxes on all 19,333, so the change is a byte-level no-op for the other 19,309.

'Sits high': refuted and inverted -- it is inset 1.44pt from the top against the peers' 0.48pt because item 14's top border is the 1.44pt h93 where theirs is 0.48pt, so it sits 0.96pt LOWER, correctly derived. The r33 region split already gives it two compartments at exactly the printed divider (v783, x 570.70-571.18) -- the same count and the same writing surface as its peers. The one real difference is that they are region inputs without maxlength rather than maxlength=1 comb slots, and that is F201's deviation class, not a defect of this cell: the source draws item 14's centavos divider and item 15's rate divider as ONE collinear run bridged through the row rule h100, spanning y 405.77-429.53, so assign_comb_anchors -- which requires a divider's whole final-visible band inside its owner -- can award it to neither row.

In build/layout/2200s-2018.layout.json the three unfilled boxes are p1c11, p1c53, p1c57, all kind="label", is_empty=false. The IR shows why: run p1t17 is '?        ' spanning x 347.47-373.87 and p1t69/p1t73 are '15        '/'17        ' spanning x 28.56-60.24 - the trailing-space advance runs straight through the checkbox rect, so lattice.py never classifies it as a field.
findings.resolution: All THREE boxes, each checked separately against HEAD: item 2 Yes [358.68, 108.12, 372.00, 119.64] -> p1c11, 1 input; item 15 (43.08, 387.96) 13.32 x 11.52 -> p1c53, kind `label` 0 inputs at HEAD, kind `field` 1 input at r20; item 17 (43.56, 406.56) 13.44 x 11.52 -> p1c57, same transition. Only the first was in the assertion's population; the other two were probed by hand at this finding's own coordinates. Measured at r20 on the tree that was written, by a checker that reads the SOURCE-derived offender box out of the r19 audit and the inputs out of the shipped index.html, and never consults the r20 audit -- so a box that cleared because its row PEER lost an input would still read as uncovered. The assertion that owns this population, `printed_box_peers_all_fillable`, goes 14 offenders on 14 of 53 forms -> 0 on 0, and audit.py is byte-identical (sha256 8d22a957...), so nothing about the check moved. Corpus input count went UP by 60; nothing was deleted. Cause: two producer bugs in lattice.py -- `GroupGeometry.span` excluded a cluster's own defining rule from its coverage, and `assign_points` placed a text run by its bounding-box centre (the run's ADVANCE), so the whitespace between "Calendar" and "Fiscal" counted as printed text inside the checkbox drawn in that gap. `glyph_ink_spans` now reads the per-character origins the IR already carries.

findings.what: The hanging indent of the Schedule 1 Description list is broken: the first line of each item starts ~5pt left of its own wrapped continuation lines, which stay at the official indent.
findings.where: Part V Schedule 1, Description column, x 82-97 pt, rows from y ~286 to ~412 pt. Clearest on item f (baseline 358.7pt) and item h; also affects a, b, c, d, e, g.
findings.evidence: 2.6x side-by-side crop: the official sets "f." then a tab-width gap so "Powdered" starts exactly above "classified" on the next line; the HTML puts "Powdered" well to the left of "classified". Ink-column measurement at 192 DPI: line 1 'P' starts at device x=244 in HTML vs 258 official, while line 2 'c' is at 257 in both - so HTML's own two lines are 13 device px (~4.9pt) out of alignment where the official is aligned to 1px. The IR carries the correct offsets (run 'f. Powdered Drinks not ' has the 'P' at offset 13.44pt from x0=82.58, i.e. 96.02pt, identical to the continuation run's x0=96.02); emit.py discards them in favour of a single letter-spacing value.

findings.what: guide.html hyphenates a URL: "www.bir.gov.ph" breaks across lines as "www.bir.-" / "gov.ph", inserting a hyphen that is not part of the address.
findings.where: forms/extra/2200t-2022/guide.html, "When and Where to File and Pay" section, last paragraph ("...(refer to www.bir.gov.ph) for the preparation..."). Same in forms/extra/2200s-2018/guide.html.

findings.what: All three Part II "Manner of Payment" checkboxes (items 13, 14, 15) have no field input, so the manner of payment cannot be marked at all.
findings.evidence: I overlaid every input/textarea with a red outline in Playwright at DPR2 and looked at the page: the item 2 Yes/No and item 12 Yes/No boxes are outlined, the three Part II boxes are not. Cause is the same as on 2200-S: the neighbouring run's trailing-space advance is wide enough to overlap the box rect, so lattice.py sees the cell as occupied.
findings.resolution: All three cited boxes carry inputs in the shipped DOM at the finding's own coordinates: p1c58 [37.0, 362.5, 50.4, 374.0] (item 13), p1c59 [224.4, 362.5, 237.8, 374.0] (item 14), p1c62 [37.0, 377.3, 50.4, 388.8] (item 15). The closure is LATE, not new: byte-comparison against HEAD~1 shows all three inputs already present in the r20 shipped tree -- the r20 checkbox-class fixes (GroupGeometry.span counting a cluster's own rule as coverage; glyph_ink_spans placing runs by ink, not advance) fixed this population and the finding was not re-verified then.

findings.what: The "Basic Excise" column header is displaced ~3.7pt to the left, so the "B" straddles the vertical column rule and butts against the ")" of "(Value/Volume of Removal)" in the neighbouring header.
findings.where: Part V Schedule 1 header band, y ~136-146 pt. Column rule at x=537.1pt; "B" starts at ~534.8pt (official ~538.5pt). Same defect repeats on page 3 (Schedule 1 - continuation) at top:125.25pt.
findings.evidence: 9x side-by-side crop: in the official the rule is clear of the B with a visible gap on both sides; in the HTML the rule cuts through the left stem of the B. Ink-column profile over the glyph band gives first HTML ink at 534.6pt vs 536.9/539.9pt official. Cause: the IR run is ' Basic Excise ' at x0=531.10 whose leading space has an advance of 7.8pt (char_origin_offsets_pt[1]=7.8), but emit.py writes it as an ordinary space plus a uniform letter-spacing:0.3938pt, so the B lands ~4pt early.

findings.what: The TIN comb fields (items 3, 12, 16) have 8 character inputs for 14 printed comb cells, three of them double-width, and typed characters land on the comb dividers instead of inside the cells.
findings.evidence: I filled every input with a distinct letter via Playwright and screenshotted. Group 1 renders 'MNOPQRS' (7 chars) crammed across all three printed cells and overflowing past the group edge into the '-' separator; group 2 shows only E and F for 3 cells with E straddling a divider; group 3 shows only G and H for 3 cells; group 4 shows I J K L for 5 cells, each sitting on a divider rather than centred. The PDF crop of the same band shows a clean 3-3-3-5 = 14-cell comb. Same test on 2200M item 1 produced a correct 2+2+4 layout, so this is form-specific, not a harness artefact.
findings.resolution: All three TIN rows (items 3, 12, 16) now print 4 comb groups of 3+3+3+5 = 14 compartments, each compartment its own maxlength-1 input: p1c17/p1c12/p1c14/p1c16 (item 3), p1c59/p1c54/p1c56/p1c58 (item 12), p1c74/p1c76/p1c78/p1c80 (item 16), read from build/layout and the shipped DOM. Screenshot with digits typed one per compartment, group separators printed between: scratchpad blockers2/F111-2316-item3-tin-r21.png (14 inputs filled, one glyph per printed cell, no character on a divider). Cause: the first TIN group's guide ticks stop 0.25pt above the box bottom (tick y1 137.62 against baseline ink 137.87), so `supported_at` filed them as borders supported at neither end and the group lost its compartments. `lattice.bottom_guide_tick_baseline` (r21) recognises the bottom-guide-tick pattern -- hangs from nothing, lands within its own stroke width of a baseline, walled on both sides on that baseline, corroborated by same-loop siblings or uniform pitch -- and classifies them as comb dividers. No tolerance was widened; a blanket y-tolerance was tried and refuted (it flips 45 real combs).

findings.what: Same leading-whitespace defect: 'Calendar', '2nd', '3rd' and the bold item number '2' before 'ATC' are painted ~3.1 pt too high and ~4-5 pt too far left, colliding with their checkboxes.
findings.evidence: Measured row ink profiles in both rasters over x 86-130: HTML 'Calendar' glyph body spans y 118.75-124.75, PDF spans 121.38-128.12 — a 3.1 pt vertical offset; 'Fiscal' (no leading space) spans 121.75-127.75 in both. Column profile over x 60-135: PDF gives checkbox [74.25-88.5] then 'C' at [92.25-97.5]; HTML merges box and 'C' into one group [74.25-92.25], i.e. the glyph touches the box, and the word is stretched to the same right edge. IR text values are '  2 ', ' Calendar', ' 2nd ', ' 3rd ' — all leading-space runs; 'ATC', 'Fiscal', '1st ' have none and are correct.
findings.resolution: emit.py anchors a padded run on its first *visible* glyph and emits its ink, instead of reproducing the padding spaces with the substitute face's own space advance plus a share of the run's smeared tracking. Measured on 2550-DS page 1: 'Calendar' was 4.90pt left of its origin, ' 2nd ' 4.50pt, ' 3rd ' 3.68pt and the bold '2' 2.27pt; all are now exact. The tracking is re-derived over the emitted glyphs from the IR's own advances, and only for a run whose ink is a single word - see Ink in emit.py.

findings.what: The BIR seal artwork is rendered vertically flipped (upside-down) — all rim lettering reads mirrored top-to-bottom and the shield is inverted.
findings.where: Seal image, x 30.48-71.28 pt, y 37.92-74.64 pt (top-left of the header box)
findings.evidence: I cropped the seal from both rasters at 7x and put a vertically-flipped copy of the PDF crop beside them: the flipped PDF matches the HTML pixel-for-pixel in shape and lettering, the unflipped PDF does not. In the official the rim reads BUREAU OF INTERNAL REVENUE / PHILIPPINES; in the HTML it reads inverted. Root cause from the data: build/ir/2550m-undated.ir.json records only {x0,y0,x1,y1} for the image with no transform/CTM field. fitz get_image_info on the source PDFs shows 2550M's placement matrix has d = -36.72 while every other form I reviewed (2200C +28.08, 2200M +28.08, 2316 +31.01, 2550-DS +39.65, 2550Q +29.70) has the opposite sign. The sign is the flip; the IR cannot carry it, so emit painted it like all the others.
findings.resolution: emit.py applies image["transform"], the full 6-element matrix, to a unit-square <image>: `transform="matrix(40.8,0,0,-36.72,30.48,74.64)"`. The flip is not special-cased - the matrix is carried, which also covers 0605's non-zero `b` - and it is applied only when its own box agrees with the extractor's to 0.005pt, so a matrix the two views could not reconcile falls back to the box. A 110dpi print-to-PDF crop of page 1 shows the seal upright with its rim lettering readable.

findings.what: All 31 solid black ► pointer markers are rendered as hollow '⌐' corner marks — the filled triangle was converted into two hairline rules along its top and left edges.
findings.where: 31 occurrences on page 1; first at x 32.88-36.96, y 27.60-31.44 pt (beside 'DLN:'). Others beside PSIC, 'For the Month of', TIN, RDO Code, Line of Business, Zip Code, 29D/30A/30C/31A/31C/32A etc.
findings.evidence: The source draws them as filled paths: fitz get_drawings reports type 'f', items ['l','l','l'], fill (0,0,0), rect [32.88, 27.6, 36.96, 31.44]. The emitted HTML contains, at exactly those coordinates, <rect x="32.88" y="27.48" width="4.08" height="0.24" data-rule-id="h0"/> and <rect x="32.76" y="27.6" width="0.24" height="3.84" data-rule-id="v188"/> — the triangle's bounding top and left edges as 0.24 pt rules, and no triangle. Visually at 12x the HTML shows a thin grey right-angle where the PDF shows a solid arrowhead. Only 2550M among my six forms has filled non-rectangular paths.
findings.resolution: emit.py renders page["paths"]; 2550M page 1 emits 175 paths of which 31 are black-filled, and the crop above shows solid black markers at 'DLN:', 'For the Month of' and every other field.

findings.what: The pre-printed '0 0 0' branch code inside the item 4 TIN field is missing from the HTML — the fourth TIN group renders empty.
findings.where: Item 4 TIN, fourth comb group; the three zeros occupy x 182.64-208.56 pt, y 123.36-131.28 pt
findings.evidence: Side-by-side crop at 8x: the PDF shows '0,0,0' in the fourth group, the HTML box is blank. The zeros are not text — page.get_text('rawdict', clip) over that rect returns only spaces, and there are no AcroForm widgets on any page. fitz get_drawings shows them as three stroked bezier paths (type 's', items ['c','c','c','c'], colour (0,0,0), width 0.72) at x 182.64, 193.44, 203.76, y 123.36-131.28. The extractor keeps only axis-aligned 're' rectangles as rules, so curve-drawn glyphs are dropped. build/ir/2550m-undated.ir.json page 1 has no text run in that band.
findings.resolution: The finding's evidence predates path extraction and emission; verified directly rather than assumed. build/ir/2550m-2007.ir.json (the slug this form now carries) page 1 records path5, path6 and path7 as stroked beziers at x 182.64 / 193.44 / 203.76, y 123.36-131.28, stroke (0,0,0), stroke_width 0.72pt - the three curve-drawn zeros the extractor used to drop - and forms/2550m-2007/index.html emits all three as <path d="M185.28 123.36C...Z" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.72"> elements starting at x 185.28, 196.08 and 206.16 with y 123.36, tagged data-path-id path5/path6/path7. The fourth TIN group is no longer blank. It remains true, as the finding says, that no text run exists in that band - the glyphs are vector paths in the source and are now carried as vector paths.

findings.what: Page 3 is an orphan near-blank page: after the ATC table was relocated to guide.html the form document still emits the page carrying only the running header and two stray rules forming a dangling open corner.

Lending Investors/Dealer In securites/Pawnshops/Pre-need Co.', VD 010 with '10. Compulsory Social Security Public Administration & Defense', VH 010 with '11. Other Community Social and Personal Service Activity', VB 010 with '12.2 Business Services (In General)'. findings.what: Page 4 is a full page of GUIDELINES AND INSTRUCTIONS but was not relocated to guide.html, unlike page 3's ATC table — the filed-form document ships two pages of reference material handling inconsistently.
findings.where: Whole page 4; heading 'BIR Form 2550M – Monthly Value-Added Tax Declaration / GUIDELINES AND INSTRUCTIONS' at approximately y 140-155 pt
findings.evidence: Screenshot of page 4 of index.html is byte-for-eye identical to PDF page 4 and consists entirely of Who shall file / When and Where to file / Penalties / Definition of Terms / Attachments. provenance.json guide.moved_from_form lists only page 3, matched on marker_pattern 'alphanumeric-tax-code'; guide_detected.inline_pages is [3]. findings.what: The same Wingdings 0xA7 bullet is emitted as a literal section sign '§' in the form document (different fallback from the guides' tofu), where the official prints a filled square.

Zoomed x 315-560 / y 725-830 at 5x: HTML shows '§' at each bullet, PDF shows '▪'. IR records these four runs as font 'Wingdings', text '§' (0xa7). The emitted markup is
§
— the pipeline knows the glyph is unresolved and substitutes a section sign.

findings.what: Row 1/3 labels are letter-spaced and shifted left into their checkboxes; 'Quarter' is overprinted by the 1st checkbox and '2nd'/'3rd' are raised ~3 pt above the row baseline and sit on top of their boxes.

findings.what: Same Wingdings tofu in guide.html: two bullets render as empty boxes instead of filled squares.

findings.what: Same lost-triangle defect: all 25 pre-printed ► pointer marks render as faint grey "⊢" hairlines instead of solid black triangles.
findings.where: 25 occurrences on page 1, e.g. x 31.2-36.24pt / y 138.96-144.0pt (item 1), x 243.84-248.88 / y 160.08-165.12 (item 3 month), x 37.44-42.48 / y 203.76-208.8 (TIN), plus the Part II "Computation of Tax" heading at approx x 196 / y 300, and every 27-30D payment row

findings.what: The relocated ATC rate table is flattened into running prose, destroying the ATC-code-to-tax-rate column association; codes, descriptions and percentages run together in continuous paragraphs.
findings.where: guide.html, the "ALPHANUMERIC TAX CODE (ATC)" section (213 text runs moved off page 2 at cut_y 154.32pt)
findings.evidence: Screenshotted the guide. The heading "ATC Percentage Tax On: Tax Rate" is emitted, then the body is one paragraph: "PT 010 Persons exempt from VAT under Sec. 109z (Sec. 116) 3% PT 040 Domestic carriers and keepers of garages 3% PT 041 International Carriers 3% PT 060 Franchises on electric utilities, gas and water utility 2% PT 070 Franchises on radio/TV broadcasting companies whose" / "annual gross receipts do not exceed P 10 M 3% Tax on banks and non-bank financial intermediaries". Later: "basis of the remaining maturities of the instrument 5%,3%,1%,0% PT 102 2) On dividends 0% PT 103 3) On royalties, rentals of property, real or personal, profits from exchange and all other gross income 5%". The sibling form 2551Q, whose ATC table was detected as cells, renders a proper two-column table - so this is a per-form regression, not an intended presentation.
findings.resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07 (r19), and this time the measurement is the association the finding names rather than the symptom it described. Measured at r20 on the tree that was written, by a checker that reads the SOURCE-derived offender box out of the r19 audit and the inputs out of the shipped index.html, and never consults the r20 audit -- so a box that cleared because its row PEER lost an input would still read as uncovered. findings.resolution: FIXED (W2), implementing P2's own measured row-number rule: PARTLY REFUTED as recorded, its SCHEDULE C half (p2c97/p2c103/p2c109) not a defect -- pre-printed deduction category names on a tint, correctly not fields -- so what remained was the Schedule D half only, p2c132/136/140/144. `emit.py` gains a `RowNumberWriting` class and a `row-number` branch in `field_verdict` (the same family shape as `RuledBlankWriting`/`CheckboxSquareWriting`/`KnockoutSpecifyWriting`): a `label` cell sharing its row with a `field` cell, holding ONLY a bare numeral (`^\d{1,3}$`, so '12' is a row number and '12.' or '(12)' is not), earns the paper beside the numeral when that trailing blank clears the form's own `line_width_pt` at 1.0x (`lattice.min_fillable_line_metrics`, the sliver rule's own metric -- no new constant) and the cell is tall enough for one line of the form's own smallest body text. All four Schedule D anchors gain an input (p2c132/136/140/144, verified typeable in a real Chromium page: goto/Tab/type/read-back, reached at tab presses 437/441/445/449 from the first input, typed and read back 'Contribution to accredited NGO' in all four). The rule's own raw claim set, re-derived corpus-wide every run by the new standing self-test `emit.row_number_corpus_assertions`, is 61 cells across 13 forms -- P2 measured 296 candidates -> 56 across 23 forms on the r38 tree, and the drop to 61/13 here is fully explained by ~35 intervening commits (F148/F149 ruled-blank, F210 checkbox-square, F211/F212 signature-box, F206 knockout-specify, and several lattice-level ink/wall/pre-printed-text fixes) that reclassify `label` cells between r38 and this tree. 12 of the 61 (2200m-2018's 4 cells, 1702mx-2018c's p2c278/p2c280 and p4c196/198/200/202/204/206) are ALREADY fillable via `RuledBlankWriting`, which landed after P2's own measurement, so the NET NEW gain this package ships is 49 cells across 11 forms: 0605-1999 stays untouched (see below), 1600-pt-2018 (5), 1600-vt-2018 (5), 1621-2019 (5), 1700-2018 (4), 1701-2018 (2), 1701-2018-conso (4, the anchors), 1702mx-2018c (4), 1702mx-2018c-attachment (8), 1702rt-2018c (8), 2200a-2020 (2), 2200p-2020 (2). Corpus-wide the rule correctly excludes all 228 narrow (13-16pt) item-number boxes sharing a row with a field cell -- P2's own 'a 14.8pt box holding 12' population, measured at 188 on the r38 tree, moved by the same tree drift -- proved unchanged as a count and by direct HTML diff (0 overlap between the 228 and the 49 gained cells). Measurement found and this package fixed a real defect before shipping: the first cut of `row_number_band` trimmed only the candidate cell's OWN leading ink and, on 0605-1999, published an input at p1c81 that landed on top of 'For the ... Calendar ... Fiscal' -- a checkbox caption assigned to a neighbouring cell whose own glyphs physically overlap p1c81's rectangle, the `printed_box_peers_all_fillable`/`assign_points` shape CLAUDE.md already documents, pointed a new way. `row_number_band` now refuses any candidate whose trailing blank carries ANY intrusion from ANY run's own ink, page-wide, not just the candidate cell's own assigned run; 0605-1999 is correctly excluded and gains nothing. `inputs_over_printed_text` (the assertion this exact defect would trip) stays at its own pre-existing 2 forms/5 offenders (1604cf-2008, 2316-2021); `comb_slots_match_printed` stays 10 forms/19; comb censuses stay 4,587 subjects/33 retained/4,554 comb cells (row-number never touches a comb cell by construction); the corpus tab-walk stays 53/53 green and the blue `vacant` census stays 108, unmoved. Input count 45,468 -> 45,520 (+52 emitted `<input>` elements; 49 net-new cells, +3 more because three of them sit in a growable band and are mirrored into that band's own `<template>` blueprint row). A new source-level mutation, `fixtures/prove_row_number` (`make_fixtures.row_number_row`, a synthetic bordered row with a bare numeral beside a blank field cell, shrunk by `prove_fixtures_fail.mutate_row_number`), proves the rule can fail: the label cell's own width narrows from 60pt to 20pt, the trailing blank drops under half of `line_width_pt`, and the claim disappears. Deliberately run outside `extract.py`'s own CASES/CONTRACT_ONLY accounting, since row-number is a `lattice.py`/`emit.py` decision with no new extract-level primitive of its own -- extract.py's own 24 checks are unmoved. `EXPECTED_HTML_STRUCTURE_SHA256` (comb_referee.py) re-pinned for the 11 forms whose `build/html/<slug>.html` bytes moved.

findings.resolution: CLOSED not-a-defect 2026-08-11 on the user's own visual review, which is the evidence this finding always needed and could not get from the content stream. The finding's item 33 half WAS a real defect and was fixed in r35 (that cell is now p1c251, kind `shaded`, no input). Its sworn-declaration half is refuted. The user loaded 1701-2018 p1 in Chromium, focused the input at p1c125 (14.88,705.34, 449.02 x 34.20 pt) and typed their full name into it, and reports the behaviour as CORRECT and wanted -- the strip sits directly above the printed caption 'Printed Name and Signature of Taxpayer/Authorized Representative', so it is the form's signature line, not decoration. A raster-only measurement of a cell that draws no fill cannot establish that the cell is decorated. What remains is not correctness but typography: the input is vertically centred in a 34.20pt strip (.fh52, line-height 33.24pt) where a signature line wants to sit at the bottom. Split out as F212 rather than kept open here, because a styling preference is not this finding's claim.

findings.what: The guide reflow silently DROPPED text. A table cell whose colspan reached a column that a later cell on the same line already owned made the row walk skip that later cell entirely, so its runs left the document with the row still looking well formed.
findings.where: tools/formgen/emit.py, `_table_markup`'s row walk. Shipped effect: forms/extra/2200an-2018/guide.html was missing '(To Part III, Item 16)' from the Schedule 1C row and two 't' glyphs elsewhere.
findings.evidence: emit.py --self-test, 'a converted guide PDF carries every run of its own extraction': 310 runs, 21 missing, once the r19 column grid made the columns narrow enough to expose it. Character-level diff of the shipped 2200-AN guide across the fix: three insertions, zero deletions.
findings.resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07 (r19) in the commit that found it. Measured on the tree that was written, after `batch.py` regenerated all 53 bundles at r19. `_table_markup` assigned each cell a colspan equal to the number of grid columns its widest run overlaps, then walked the row by stepping `index += span`. When a run crossed into a column that a LATER run on the same line started in, the walk stepped straight past that column's index and the cell was never emitted, taking its runs out of the document. emit.py's own 'a converted guide PDF carries every run of its own extraction' check found it the moment the r19 grid made narrower columns: 310 runs, 21 missing. In the shipped corpus it was live on 2200-AN, whose guide was missing 20 characters -- '(To Part III, Item 16)', the pointer that tells a filer where Schedule 1C's total goes, plus two 't' glyphs. The fix clamps a colspan so it cannot reach a column that owns a cell of its own; content is never dropped, only the span narrows. Proven three ways: the run census above passes; a new unit assertion in emit.py's self-test drives the exact shape ('a run crossing into an occupied column does not swallow its cell'); and a character-level diff of the shipped `forms/extra/2200an-2018/guide.html` before and after shows three insertions ('t', 't', ')(ToPartIII,Item16') and ZERO deletions, 13,228 -> 13,248 dense characters. Rebuilding 2200-AN with and without the clamp isolates it: the table shapes are identical (79 and 74 rows either way), the clamped build is 836 bytes larger.

findings.resolution: CLOSED by F208 in r46, and NOT by moving any of the six combs. The contradiction recorded here was between two things measured against different quantities: outer slot_x (a rail CENTRE) compared to the source rail's centre, while every emitted slot had to stay inside the owning cell. Where a printed rail's centre falls outside its owner's fused edge that pair is unsatisfiable -- but the rail's own INK EDGE lies inside the rectangle, and that is what an outer compartment is actually bounded by. With writing_x0/writing_x1 published and both outer relations retargeted onto the rails' ink, all six hold: 1701MS p1c166/p1c173/p1c179/p1c187, 2550M p1c203, 2550Q p1c6. comb_slots_match_printed 12 forms/25 -> 10 forms/19, its decided residual is ZERO, and the 19 remaining are the same source-unevaluable subjects cell for cell and reason for reason -- nothing new appeared. findings.what: 42 cells that the source rules across are now emitted as several WRITING REGIONS of one field (-i0, -i1, ...) rather than as combs. For the cells whose dividers are bottom guide ticks -- one character per compartment -- a comb is very likely the correct model: a comb enforces one character per box (maxlength=1 per slot) where a region accepts free text. The region model was chosen partly because EXPECTED_COMBS / EXPECTED_COMB_SUBJECTS must not move without review, i.e. a census pin constrained the model rather than following it.
findings.evidence: I read build/layout/1600wp-2010.layout.json myself: p1c64 publishes three printed_partitions at x 89.88-90.13, 100.93-101.18, 110.89-111.14, each 0.25pt wide and 1.80pt tall at the cell's foot. Real ink, and one input across four printed compartments was wrong -- so the split is an improvement either way. But 1600WP was reported by NO assertion (the judge's DIVIDER_MIN_HEIGHT_PT is 2.0 and these ticks are 1.80pt), so this change was made outside the judged scope and its field model has had no independent check. Matters for stage 3: -i0/-i1 region ids are a different field identity from a comb's slot indexes.

findings.resolution: The seven horizontal offenders are NOT movable from emit.py, proved by experiment rather than by reading, and my scheduling caveat here was incomplete: it named only 2551M/2553 as possibly frozen, but ALL SEVEN ARE COMBS -- 0605 p1c3 is a 2-compartment MM|YYYY box with a 3.63pt foot tick at x 95.265-96.015. The physical fact under all seven: every offending glyph's ink STOPS SHORT OF THE WALL'S INNER EDGE. The 'C' of 28C inks to 239.5176 inside a wall painted 238.9200-239.6400 -- tucked under the printed rule, with no blank paper between the label and the wall. The writing surface begins at 239.64. The mechanism is that comb.slot_x runs WALL-CENTRE to WALL-CENTRE, so a comb's outer compartments are laid across half of each wall's own ink; lattice.comb_writing_surface already applies exactly this inset VERTICALLY (writing_y0 = cell.y0 + top) and nobody applies it horizontally. Corpus scope: 4,554 combs, 4,191 flush left with the cell edge, 4,115 flush right, 3,781 both. Trimming slot 0 by the measured overlap and re-auditing proves the trade is strictly negative -- 2551M p1c74 takes inputs_over 3->2 but comb_slots 2->3, and 0605 p1c3 takes inputs_over 1->0 but turns a HOLDING comb assertion red -- both failing on emission-layout-outer-position-mismatch against a 0.0002pt pin. Yet under that same trim EVERY SOURCE-DERIVED check still passes (emission_source_outer_position, layout_source_outer_position, emission_source_position, all within 0.25pt), so the geometry is right against the SOURCE and wrong only against slot_x, which emit does not own. The fix is F208. CLOSED by F208 in r46. The seven horizontal offenders are gone: inputs_over_printed_text 6 forms/13 -> 3 forms/6, measured corpus-wide on a regenerated tree. comb.slot_x no longer bounds an emitted compartment; comb.writing_x0/writing_x1 do, and they are the printed rails' own ink edges. 0605 p1c3, 2551M p1c74/79/86 and 2553 p1c79/84/91 all clear -- the mechanism this finding identified was exactly right, and it was not fixable from emit because emit does not own slot_x. The six survivors are this finding's other two groups, correctly untouched because neither is a horizontal placement: genuine descenders (1604CF p1c16, 2316 p1c38/p1c39) and outline overshoots past the face's declared descender (2316 p1c62/p1c83, 1701MS p1c287).

findings.what: F148/F149's fix is BLOCKED by a genuine conflict between two rules that are each correct on their own, and I reverted a working implementation rather than resolve it by editing the judge. A run of underscores is the sheet drawing a writing line -- it is the one ink signal in the corpus that INVITES typing, where every other one forbids it. But an input placed on that line necessarily overlaps a pre-printed text run's bbox, which is exactly what the assertion inputs_over_printed_text forbids.

findings.what: audit.py's source U-frame reader does not account for a WALL splitting a printed frame, so it reports three false offenders under comb_slots_match_printed: 'claimed comb owner crops a wider source U-frame'. The forms are right and the audit is wrong.
