findings.evidence: Settled from the pinned source's own operators by the operator, not inferred. 2000-DST p1 x 164.30-248.69 carries THREE full-height 0.48pt verticals (x 164.06, 192.14, 248.45; y 109.70-129.02, height 19.32pt) and FOUR short 0.24pt ticks (x 178.22, 206.45, 220.49, 234.53; y 121.10-129.02, height 7.92pt). The stroke at 192.14 is twice the thickness and 2.4x the height of every divider in the band, i.e. a wall by the same measure lattice already uses. The sheet corroborates: the white knockout of the top rule is drawn as TWO spans, 164.54-192.14 and 192.62-248.45, stopping at the wall on each side -- a single frame would have been erased in one span. So the source prints two boxes of 2 and 4 compartments, exactly what is emitted, and the audit's reading of one wider U-frame is the defect. Fixing it means teaching _source_u_frame that a full-height wall of border weight partitions a frame.
findings.resolution: FIXED in r44 in audit.py, the judge -- the forms were right throughout. _source_u_frame already partitioned a frame at walls via _carries_band_into_rule_above, but on these three subjects that witness is defeated because the sheet ERASES THE WALL JUST ABOVE THE BAND, so an erased wall looks exactly like 2200-A's knocked-out DIVIDER and the walk failed closed. Where ink presence above the cut decides nothing, the sheets separate the two cases on HOW THE STROKES ARE DRAWN, on two axes and never one: a wall is strictly thicker than the thinnest stroke standing between the same two rails AND stands strictly higher than every one of them, with 'how high a stroke stands' walked upward from the band through same-tone paint confined to that stroke's own ink width, crossing a break only when the break is fully covered by opaque paint also confined to that width. An erasure cut to one stroke is that stroke's own edit; a grey band crossing the same x on its way elsewhere is not. Measured separation: 2000-DST's dividers are 4 x 0.24pt standing 1.08pt above the band against a 0.48pt stroke standing 12.00pt; 2200-C 1 x 0.24pt at 1.08pt against 0.48pt at 10.80pt; and the two negative controls have NO separation at all -- 2200-A's erased divider 0.24 vs 0.24, 2551-M 0.72 vs 0.72. A THIRD CLAUSE WAS FORCED BY A REGRESSION THE AGENT CAUGHT ITSELF: the comparison is refused outright unless the dividers stand above the band, because 2200-C's money rows carry real 0.48pt column walls beside digit dividers flush with the band, and without it the money comb was cut and 60 NEW offenders appeared. That clause is now a mutation, so it cannot be quietly removed. Verified by the operator on this tree: comb_slots_match_printed 28 -> 25, the three cells gone (2000-DST's offenders are now only p1c109, 2200C's only p1c107 -- both pre-existing competing-topology cases), inputs_over_printed_text unmoved at 6 forms/13, both zero families still 0, and ZERO shipped bytes moved. 6 new fixtures and 6 new mutations, each verified to trip its own check on a scratch copy. Two cells deliberately NOT forced: 2551m-2002 p1c82 and 2553-1999 p1c87, where every interior vertical is drawn at one weight (0.72pt, box walls and compartment ticks alike), so no stroke is strictly thicker than the thinnest and the relation correctly refuses -- a different defect needing a different witness.

findings.what: The real 'a caption on ink the cell does not hold' population -- the honest remainder of the refuted F203 -- is 61 cells across 14 forms, defined by the strict test: no ink whose BASELINE sits on the cell's own paper. 60 of the 61 are already kind 'shaded' (thin strips of grey band offset from their caption line), so they are correctly non-fields for the wrong reason and have zero fillability impact. Exactly ONE is a genuine missing field: 1801-2018 p2c261 'Others (specify)'. Recorded separately from F203 because that finding was a measurement artifact and this one is not.
findings.evidence: Measured on a corpus regenerated at HEAD. Two independent source measures agree 60/1 in both directions: of the 61, 60 are shaded by the producer's own >=70% rule, and exactly 1 (1801 p2c261) carries an ink-free knockout band of at least the form's own line_width_pt. ALSO RECORDED HERE, because it is the route rather than a defect: the part-caption/part-writing-surface family that F148/F149/F151 all belong to IS bounded by a source-published marker -- the widest ink-free band whose topmost paint is a KNOCKOUT over a decorative tint, at >= 1x the form's own line_width_pt. That selects 61 cells / 19 forms with an 11x separation (0.09x -> 1.01x), and the gap is NOT empty: 8 named cells sit in it (0605 p2c58/p2c121, 2553 p1c37/42/47/52, 1600wp p1c30/33), all ATC-code or rate cells on reference tables and none a writing surface. So it is a marker with a reviewable residue, not a decision procedure. Dropping the 'over a tint' requirement destroys it (123 cells, mostly white-on-white reference tables): a knockout only means something where there is a band to knock out. The right implementation is a CELL SPLIT at the knockout boundary -- the writing surface is a sub-region -- not a reclassification of the whole cell.
findings.resolution: FIXED in W1 by giving a label cell an input when its own paper carries a knockout-over-tint band beside a "(specify)" caption. emit.py gains KnockoutSpecifyWriting / knockout_specify_band / knockout_specify_field_box, following RuledBlankWriting / CheckboxSquareWriting / SignatureBoxWriting's own shape exactly: the writing surface is a sub-region of the cell, never a reclassification of it (F206's own conclusion), and lattice.py is untouched -- the split is emit-side because that is where every sibling promotion in this family already lives, and F206's own population is dominated by 'shaded' kind cells that must keep their existing, correct verdict unchanged. The marker as measured: the widest ink-free rectangle within the cell whose topmost paint is role=="knockout", where "ink-free" excludes this cell's own assigned text runs by their WHOLE line box (not per glyph -- an ATC code's inter-character gaps are not writable paper), gated on the cell carrying a MEANINGFUL knockout fill AND a MEANINGFUL decorative fill somewhere in its own paper (clipped overlap > KNOCKOUT_FILL_MEANINGFUL_OVERLAP_PT, 1.5pt, extract.MAX_RULE_THICKNESS_PT restated, on both axes -- a hairline graze from a neighbouring row's own background is not this cell's own tint) and on the band clearing the form's own two-glyph line width and cap-height. Two refinements past F206's own prose, both forced by measurement against the named residue -- see knockout_specify_band's own docstring. A caption vocabulary gate is ALSO required: the joined caption must contain "specify" (case-insensitive), BIR's own invitation to free text. This was not in F206's own definition but was forced by measurement: the pure geometric marker (no caption test) selects on the order of 90+ label cells across the corpus, the large majority NOT writing surfaces -- 1604CF's 11-run table headers, 2550M's near-full-width declaration bands, 2553's "OT  0   1   0"-style ATC captions with wide but non-writable margins -- none reviewed by any finding, and giving all of them an input would be exactly the unreviewed mass promotion F206 itself warns against ("a marker with a reviewable residue, not a decision procedure"). Requiring "specify" narrows the promoted population to 23 cells across 11 forms, every one a genuine "Other ___ (specify)" or "Others (specify below)" free-text invitation, the same caption-driven idiom this file already uses everywhere else a label cell is promoted (SIGNATURE_BOX_CAPTION_PREFIXES, BUREAU_RESERVED_PREFIXES, _signature_line_caption's "signature"+"printed name" test). Of those 23, 22 ALREADY carried an input from RuledBlankWriting (checked first in field_verdict's rule order, so KnockoutSpecifyWriting never runs for them) -- among them 1801-2018 p2c261 itself, F206's own named example. Measured directly: p2c261 already has a working <input>, seated on an underscore-drawn rule at x93.73-377.36 (RULE_ORIGIN_TEXT_UNDERSCORE, role structural), fixed independently by T5c/RuledBlankWriting (gate r50, 2026-08-11) in the interval between F206's filing (2026-07-29) and this package. Verified in a real Chromium page: build/html/1801-2018.html, #p2c261-i reached at Tab press 899, typed "123456" and read back correctly. Exactly ONE cell gains a NEW input: 1801-2018 p1c197, "Others  (specify) " (item 24, page 1) -- the same "part caption, part writing surface" shape as p2c261 but on a different row, where the decorative tint (411.91-471.7pt) and the knockout (516.82-584.38pt) are drawn as two rectangles tiling one row, the same tri-partition technique p2c261's own row uses. Verified in a real Chromium page: #p1c197-i reached at Tab press 256, typed "123456" and read back correctly. The box is seated exactly on the knockout's own rectangle (inset trbl 0/4.32pt/0/46.58pt against the 118.42x7.78pt cell). The 8 residue cells F206 named -- 0605-1999 p2c58/p2c121, 2553-1999 p1c37/p1c42/p1c47/p1c52, 1600wp-2010 p1c30/p1c33 -- are unchanged, proven two ways: none carries "specify" in its caption (checked directly, false in every case, so KnockoutSpecifyWriting never constructs a band for them regardless of geometry), and independently the pure geometric band width for each is measured at or below the form's own line width (0605 p2c58 and 1600wp's two cells: no band at all past the meaningful-overlap gate; 0605 p2c121 and 2553's four cells: 0.78x to 0.91x). Neither test alone would be enough (the geometric ratio is close for the 2553 cells; the caption test says nothing about geometry) -- together they give two independent reasons the residue stays refused. Measured against the corpus (build/ir + build/layout regenerated fresh, batch.py run twice, byte-identical): inputs_over_printed_text stays 2 forms/5 offenders (1604cf-2008, 2316-2021), comb_slots_match_printed stays 10 forms/19 offenders, comb censuses stay 4,587 subjects/33 retained/4,554 active cells (lattice.py is byte-identical, so the ledger cannot have moved). Input count 45,467 -> 45,468 (+1). Corpus tab-walk 53/53 green (118.2s); the corpus-wide blue/vacant census stays 108, unmoved, per-form identical to the prior round -- p1c197 was never in it, because the overlay's vacant test already skips any printed box containing text, exactly the F211 precedent. A standing corpus-wide self-test (emit.knockout_specify_corpus_assertions, run by `emit.py --self-test`) re-derives the 23-cell claim set against every build/ir + build/layout + build/fonts triple this checkout has and fails if any claimed cell lacks a typing surface (bands_checked > 0 is asserted too); it also cross-checks the restated `_min_fillable_line_metrics` (emit.py carries no import of lattice.py) against `lattice.min_fillable_line_metrics` directly on every form, so the two cannot silently drift. Five paired positive/negative fixture assertions (emit.knockout_specify_writing_assertions) prove the caption gate, the meaningful-overlap gate and the whole-run-bbox ink block can each independently fail, using synthetic geometry mirroring the named residue's own shape; field_verdict routes a claim through a dedicated "knockout-specify" reason, asserted end to end. Deliberately left alone, both measured and reported rather than improvised. F065 (1707-2021 item 9): the marker does NOT reach it. The knockout is real (471.82-583.66 x 351.53-360.89, matching the finding's own coordinates exactly) and sits on a meaningful decorative tint, but the caption run carrying "(please specify)" ALSO carries the unresolved underscore sequence (F065's own standing, correct refusal -- unembedded Arial Narrow, no substitutable face), so that run's own bounding box -- blocked whole, not per glyph, which is what keeps 2553's ATC captions out -- covers virtually the entire knockout, leaving no candidate band past the meaningful-overlap floor. F065's other barrier is untouched. F221 (12 signature areas, 6 forms): the GEOMETRIC half of the marker does reach 6 of the 12 (0605-1999 p1c176, 1604cf-2008 p1c316, 2550m-2007 p1c181, 2551m-2002 p1c175, 2553-1999 p1c216, 2316-2021 p1c337; measured directly with knockout_specify_band's own caption test bypassed, bands 29x-52x each form's own line width) -- these ARE the same tint/knockout tri-partition shape. But none carries "specify": every one is "I declare, under the penalties of perjury..." or "Date Signed", so the caption gate this package ships never claims them, correctly -- a signature area needs SignatureLineBinding's bottom-seated, centred treatment, not a generic left-anchored text box, and building that here would be the "second mechanism" the task named and forbade. Left for W4 with this measurement as its starting point; 2316-2021 p1c328/p1c339 return no band at all and p1c326 is kind=blank, not label. Not attempted: extending fixtures/prove_fixtures_fail.py (the extract.py-scoped PDF-mutation harness F210/F211 both extended) with a new pinned geometric fact from one of extract.py's 7 real official PDFs. Checked all 7 (2551Q, 0605, 1604E, 2550M, 2553, 2316, 1701) directly against the shipped KnockoutSpecifyWriting -- none contains a cell this mechanism claims, so there is no real fact in that corpus to pin. The mutation proof instead lives entirely in emit.py's own self-test (knockout_specify_writing_assertions), the same paired-assertion idiom this file already uses for F147/F210/F211's own field_verdict branches; every geometric primitive the mechanism reads (fill role/tone, glyph/run geometry) is already exhaustively proven by extract.py's existing checks (tone, general geometry fidelity), so no new extraction-side contract exists for that harness to mutate.

findings.what: Two 584pt-wide inputs are laid over printed text, and TWO independent box-geometry tests miss them for the same reason. The runs' baselines sit inside the strip, but each run was assigned to the cell ABOVE by box centre (lattice.py:5647), and emit's protective belt then fails to see them because PrePrintedInk requires half the run's BOX HEIGHT inside the cell (emit.py:1553-1567) and gets only 39% and 47% against a 0.5 threshold -- so coverage reads 0.0 and the input is allowed.
findings.where: 1701a-2018 p1c227 over the printed second line 'of deduction', and p2c208 over '[available if gross sales/receipts ... (P3M)]'.
findings.evidence: Found by running the run-assignment mechanism backwards over the corpus: 196 cells hold ink whose baseline is on their paper while owning no run of their own, 35 of those emit an input, and 33 of the 35 are slivers of 1.44pt or less. These two are the real ones. Both failures are the same shape as the refuted F203 -- a box-geometry proxy standing in for where the ink actually is -- but here the proxy lets a defect THROUGH rather than inventing one.
findings.resolution: FIXED. emit.PrePrintedInk._spans_over now admits a run when half its INK BAND is inside the cell OR its baseline is inside, using a new _ink_band(run) that reads the per-run glyph_ink_em published by extract's outline reader. The threshold itself is untouched -- PREPRINTED_COVERAGE stays 0.5 -- because the defect was never the threshold but the quantity measured against it: the old test used the run's BOX height, whose top is the face's ascent line and whose bottom is its descent line, so a run of capitals sitting on a cell's paper scored 39% and 47% 'inside' while all of its actual ink was inside. This is the same shape as the five other defects logged this session -- an outer bound taken from a nominal edge instead of measured from the ink -- and it is the sixth. Measured on the tree actually written: 1701A p1c227 and p2c208 lose their inputs (corpus 45,335 -> 45,333) and both cells now emit class="c" + data-preprinted="true"; every other document in the corpus is byte-identical; cell count 393 -> 393 on 1701A; comb censuses unmoved at 4,587 subjects / 33 retained / 4,554 comb cells with the same 369 compartments refused before and after, measured per compartment rather than assumed because the same 'printed in' test is shared with slot_constant/slot_caption. 1701A's form.css loses .fh0 (0.61pt) and .fh1 (1.06pt), which existed only for these two inputs: writing_box_clear_of_printed_ink had already trimmed each to a 584pt-wide typing surface 0.61pt tall lying across printed text -- unusable, and the reason check_inputs_over_printed_text never saw it (F207 is audit_blind, and the assertion count is unchanged at 3 forms / 6 offenders because it never counted these two). comb_referee EXPECTED_HTML_STRUCTURE_SHA256 re-pinned for 1701a-2018 only, with the cause recorded above the pin; comb_referee --self-test passes on the written tree.

findings.what: A comb has no HORIZONTAL writing surface. comb.slot_x runs wall-centre to wall-centre, so every comb's outer compartments are laid across half of each printed wall's own ink. The vertical twin of this was fixed long ago -- lattice.comb_writing_surface insets the band to writing_y0/writing_y1 -- and the horizontal analogue was never written. This is the sixth instance in this codebase of one shape: an outer bound taken from a nominal edge instead of measured from the ink.
findings.where: 4,554 combs corpus-wide; 4,191 flush left with the cell edge, 4,115 flush right, 3,781 both. It is what blocks the seven horizontal offenders of F199 (0605 p1c3, 2551M p1c74/79/86, 2553 p1c79/84/91) and is the same freeze F196 records.
findings.evidence: Measured, with the design and its safety margins established rather than sketched. (1) NO TOLERANCE NEEDS TO MOVE: audit.source_frame_geometry already publishes left_rail/right_rail ink_x0/ink_x1, so only the comparison TARGET changes -- outer edges against the rail's INK edge instead of its centre. Reusing slot_x for both jobs is what cannot work: the half-wall inset is 0.36-0.48pt and 38.7% of the 8,306 flush outer edges exceed POSITION_TOL_PT = 0.25 against the centre. (2) IT CLEARS ALL SEVEN WITH MARGIN: slot 0 on the left rail's ink edge gives 0.1224pt clearance on 2551M and 2553 and 0.3006pt on 0605, all above OVERLAP_EPS_PT = 0.05. (3) NOTHING BECOMES UNUSABLE: insetting every comb in the corpus to its walls' ink leaves a narrowest outer compartment of 6.12pt (1604CF p1c30), nothing under 6pt -- this is NOT the 2550M trade that was reverted for costing a fitted face. A second change is required alongside it: audit.input_boxes scores the SLOT DIV and never the input's own inset, so today any producer-side fix inside a slot is unscoreable by the judge.
findings.resolution: FIXED in r46. lattice.comb_rails reports each outer rail's own painted ink beside its position, measured from exactly the bars that established that position; comb_on_writing_surface insets slot_x's outer values to those ink edges and publishes writing_x0/writing_x1/writing_width_pt, with writing_x_rails naming what derived each side. slot_x, divider_x, the compartment counts and the pitch are UNTOUCHED -- two questions, two sets of keys, exactly as the vertical twin leaves y0/y1 alone. emit.comb_slot_edges is the single emit-side reader (slot div, input, and the band-template JSON a cloned row is re-laid from); comb_referee.emitted_geometry_contract and gate._emission_geometry_from_layout stay two INDEPENDENT re-derivations and moved together. NO TOLERANCE MOVED: POSITION_TOL_PT 0.25 and EMITTED_GEOMETRY_EPS_PT 0.0002 are unchanged; only the comparison target moved from a rail's centre to its inner ink edge, i.e. an inner edge against an inner edge. Verified by the operator on the regenerated tree: inputs_over_printed_text 6 forms/13 -> 3 forms/6, comb_slots_match_printed 12 forms/25 -> 10 forms/19 with its DECIDED RESIDUAL AT ZERO, both zero families still 0. 4,546 of 4,554 combs get a measured inset on both rails (insets 0.01/0.24/0.96pt min/median/max); 8 FAIL CLOSED to slot_x on at least one side because no bar of that rail crosses the band -- 1700 p1c21/p1c68, 1707 p2c38, 2000-DST p1c4/p1c5, 2200C p1c7/p1c11/p1c13 -- counted rather than guessed, and 0 surrender to a degenerate width. Narrowest resulting outer compartment 6.12pt (1604CF p1c30), nothing under 6pt, and NO fitted face moved -- proved rather than argued, the <input> attribute multiset is byte-identical in all 53 documents, because a comb's size is fitted to its writing HEIGHT and capped at the sheet's body size, never to slot width. That is what separates this from the 2550M trade reverted in r33. Companion change landed with it: audit.input_boxes now reads a comb input's own declared inset instead of scoring its slot div, so a producer-side move inside a slot is visible to the judge in both directions. Census unmoved: 4,587 subjects, 33 retained, 4,554 comb cells, 45,494 inputs, zero input delta. All 53 documents move and all 53 EXPECTED_HTML_STRUCTURE_SHA256 are re-pinned with a structural review recorded (tag inventory, visible text and input attributes identical in every one); HTML_RUNTIME_SCRIPT_SHA256 does not move. 18 mutations across five files, 18 caught, none tripping an unrelated check. NO horizontal Poppler corroboration was added, deliberately and with the reason in the docstring: the vertical band needed one because it is a RELATION between two lattice-asserted numbers, whereas these edges are the rails' own painted ink, which audit.py already measures independently through its own parser and binds per comb at POSITION_TOL_PT -- a second re-derivation would duplicate that check and would compare absolute coordinates between two rasterisers at 1e-9, where the vertical compares a THICKNESS and tolerates a sub-point offset. The one consequence outside the change, fill_check.py deriving expected slot centres from slot_x and so naming 2,046 of 9,108 outer-compartment centres as bad landings that are not real, was applied by the operator in the same commit.

findings.what: Keyboard tab order does not follow the printed reading order on any form with a growable band -- 22 of 53 forms; this entry is anchored at the worst measured exemplar. Every band's rows are emitted AFTER the entire static field layer, so a user tabbing down a page reaches the bottom and is then thrown back UP to the band's rows, which sit mid-page. The user hit this by hand and described it exactly: 'sometimes I already finished the form and it went back up again'.
findings.where: emit.py:5677 closes <div class="layer-cells"> and emit.py:5680-5698 then appends every <template> + <div class="band" id="band-content-..."> after it. Worst measured case 1600-pt-2018 p1: DOM neighbours p1c195 (top 829.0pt) -> p1c50 (top 338.9pt), a 490pt jump backwards, and p1c50 is a confirmed member of band p1g0 in the layout.
findings.evidence: Corpus scan of all 53 shipped forms/<slug>/index.html against build/layout/*.layout.json: 128 same-page DOM-order inversions in 47 forms, of which the band class is the systemic one; 22 of 53 forms have growable bands. Independently, the layout cell arrays are in exact (y0,x0) reading order with ZERO inversions, so the layout is right and the emission order is what is wrong. No tabindex attribute exists anywhere in tools/ or in any shipped document, so focus order IS DOM order.
findings.resolution: FIXED in T1 (gate r47). The field layer is now split into `layer-cells` segments around each growable band, so a band is emitted at its own (y0,x0) instead of after the page's entire static cell layer. No `tabindex` was added and none exists in the corpus -- focus order is DOM order, and the layout's cell arrays were already in exact reading order, so emission order was the whole defect. Measured on the written tree: reading-order inversions **3,363 across 20 forms -> 0 across all 53**, with rows clustered the way band_drive.row_tops does rather than by a fixed epsilon (sub-point row drift is real and a fixed tolerance misclassifies it both ways). Inputs unchanged at 45,333 at the time; no cell id, class, attribute or inline style moved; assertions and comb censuses unmoved; determinism byte-identical. Independently confirmed twice: by the new tab_check.py walk (53/53 green, and 20 of the 22 band forms red before the fix -- the two exceptions genuinely have their band at the page bottom), and by re-deriving the backwards jump per band form directly from the shipped HTML, which agreed with the walk on all 22. The user's own report is the acceptance test and it passes: tabbing 1701 no longer jumps back up the page.

findings.what: The Part V Schedule 1 'Taxpayer' / 'Spouse' checkbox squares are printed on the official sheet but are not fillable and are not even segmented as cells. The user could not tab into them; the ?debug=fields overlay marks them blue (printed box with no input), and those blue marks are REAL, not overlay phantoms.
findings.evidence: Read from build/ir/1701-2018.ir.json p2: the squares are drawn by rules h165 h169 h170 h172 v236 v241 and h174 h176 h179 h181 v235 v240, each 0.72pt at gray 0.251. lattice.tone_role (lattice.py:200) calls gray>0.15 decorative, and lattice.py:6295 builds the grid from structural rules only, so no lattice line exists at x 31.08/43.08 or y 360/371/381 and the whole 74x32pt area collapses to one cell. That cell holds glyph runs ('Taxpayer', '1', 'Spouse') so classify_cell returns `label` (lattice.py:3557) and field_verdict refuses at emit.py:2326 before any shading or bureau test runs. The source's own intent is recorded next to the rules: white KNOCKOUT fills at [31.44,359.76,42.72,370.56] and [31.44,370.32,42.72,381.12] paint the square interiors back to paper.
findings.resolution: FIXED in T5a by recognising a checkbox square directly rather than admitting mid-tone rules into the lattice (candidate (ii) was measured and rejected: 0.502/0.651 tones alone occupy 11/26 forms, far outside review). emit.py gains checkbox_square_boxes(), which finds every closed box of four DECORATIVE rules (role=='decorative') whose interior carries a KNOCKOUT fill (role=='knockout'), 4-20pt on both axes, matched to each frame rule by that rule's OWN half-thickness (the knockout is painted to the frame's inner edge, so the deviation is exactly half the stroke, measured at 0.24pt on every 0.48pt frame and 0.36pt on every 0.72pt one, no spread). CheckboxSquareWriting binds each square to the one 'label' cell that contains it (mirroring RuledBlankWriting), field_verdict gains a 'checkbox-square' branch reachable only for 'label' cells, and checkbox_square_field_box gives each square its own single-character <input> region (the same plain-field markup and CSS class every other field uses -- no new element, attribute or class). Corpus-wide this selects exactly 22 squares on exactly 3 forms -- 1700-2018 (14), 1701-2018 (6: the four Schedule-1 Taxpayer/Spouse boxes p2c54/p2c59 this finding named, plus item 8's two Foreign-Tax-Credit Yes/No boxes p2c36), 1701a-2018 (2, p2c139) -- independently corroborated by the tone-aware overlay's own vacant census (6/14/2, a completely different code path over the rendered SVG). 11 label cells gain an input, 22 <input> elements are added. Verified in a real Chromium page: forms/1701-2018/index.html, all six squares reachable by Tab in reading order (p2c36-i0/-i1 at presses 705/706, p2c54-i0/-i1 -- the item-1 Taxpayer/Spouse pair -- at 732/733, p2c59-i0/-i1 -- item 2 -- at 799/800), each typed into and read back correctly. inputs_over_printed_text stays 3 forms/6, comb_slots_match_printed stays 10/19, comb censuses stay 4,587/33/4,554; forms/review/<slug>/tab.json's vacant census drops by exactly 22 (1700-2018 14->0, 1701-2018 6->0, 1701a-2018 2->0; corpus total 130->108, the remaining 108 being wide ruled-blank-row tables, a different class). tab_check.py stays 53/53 green (0 red-skipped, 0 red-order on every form) with every new input in reading order. Input count 45,391 -> 45,413. A standing corpus-wide self-test (emit.checkbox_square_corpus_assertions, run by `emit.py --self-test`) re-derives this claim set on every build/ir this checkout has and fails if any claimed square's cell has no typing surface.

findings.what: The sworn-declaration signature boxes take no input at all -- the user cannot focus anywhere in them -- and the overlay does not flag it either, so the defect is invisible to both the reviewer and the debug tooling.
findings.evidence: Each box's only printed ink is one 8.97pt caption run at its top-left corner ('For Individual: ' / 'For Non-Individual: '), which sets is_empty=False, so classify_cell returns `label` (lattice.py:3557) and field_verdict refuses at emit.py:2326 -- one caption run costs a 302x43pt writing surface. The control is 0620-2019 p1c87 (17.62,506.71, 576.12x35.64pt): the SAME signature box with no caption printed inside it, is_empty=True, border_count=4, classified `field` and shipping one input today. Identical geometry, opposite outcome, one caption run apart. The overlay is silent because its `vacant` test (emit.py:5297-5330) skips any printed box containing text -- correct in general, blind here.
findings.resolution: FIXED in T5b by recognising a bordered box whose only printed ink is a top-left caption dedicating it to the taxpayer's own signature. emit.py gains SignatureBoxWriting, which selects a 'label' cell with border_count>=3, at least 20x100pt, whose text runs are all confined to the top 40% of its own height (SIGNATURE_BOX_CAPTION_BAND) and whose joined caption starts with 'For Individual:' or 'For Non-Individual:'. field_verdict gains a 'signature-box' branch reachable only for 'label' cells and routed through the existing BureauReservation check before promoting (not around it -- the ordering trap this finding named), and signature_box_field_box seats the writing surface in the remainder below the caption. The bordered-box population this rule is even asked about is 126 cells corpus-wide, not one family: 54 are the taxpayer's own boxes (this fix's claim, 27 forms, exactly two per form), 71 are Bureau-only stamp/validation boxes already recognised by BureauReservation's own captions ('Machine Validation...', 'Stamp of Receiving Office/AAB...', 'Stamp of Authorized Agent Bank...') and never claimed here because the two caption vocabularies share no word, and 1 (1600wp-2010 p1c93) is neither -- the plain column-number header '(8)' of a table, wide only because it is the table's last column and runs to the page's right margin; it matches no caption prefix and keeps its 'label' verdict untouched. Measured: 54 label cells gain an input on exactly 27 forms, 0 of the 71 Bureau boxes gain one (a standing corpus-wide self-test, emit.signature_box_corpus_assertions, re-derives both halves against every build/ir this checkout has). 0620-2019 p1c87 -- the control this finding named, the same box with no caption printed inside it -- is unchanged: still kind=field, still classified 'field', not one of the 54 new claims. Verified in a real Chromium page: forms/0619e-2018/index.html, p1c87-i and p1c88-i reached by Tab at presses 309/310, each typed into and read back correctly; forms/0619f-2018/index.html, p1c100-i/p1c101-i at 336/337; forms/0620-2019/index.html, p1c87-i still reached at press 309 and still typeable; a named Bureau box (0619e-2018 p1c139, 'Machine Validation/Revenue Official Receipt Details') confirmed to hold zero <input> elements. tab_check.py stays 53/53 green (0 red-skipped, 0 red-order) with every new input in reading order; the corpus vacant census stays 108 (unmoved). inputs_over_printed_text moves from 3 forms/6 to 2 forms/5 -- explained, not hidden: 1701MS p1c287, one of the F212 (T5d) bottom-seat targets landed in the same package, moved off the printed run it grazed at 0.0000pt clearance purely as a side effect of being re-seated to a one-line strip at its own cell's bottom; the other five offenders (1604CF p1c16; 2316 p1c38/p1c39/p1c62/p1c83) are untouched. comb_slots_match_printed stays 10/19, comb censuses stay 4,587/33/4,554. Input count 45,413 -> 45,467 (+54). extract.py gains a 'signature-box' self-test check pinning the geometric fact the recognition depends on (a caption confined to a box's own top 40%), against 2551Q page 1's 'For Individual:' box; a matching synthetic shape in fixtures/rules.pdf backs it with its own source-level mutation proving the check can fail. EXPECTED_HTML_STRUCTURE_SHA256 re-pinned for the 43 slugs T5b+T5d together move; AUDIT_DEPENDENCY_SHA256['tools/formgen/extract.py'] re-pinned for the self-test-only change (build/ir byte-identical to a re-extraction, verified directly on 2551Q).

findings.form: 1701-2018 (+ every form with a signature strip)
findings.what: Signature-line inputs are vertically centred in their box instead of seated at the bottom, and are left-aligned instead of centred. On a line captioned 'Signature over Printed Name' the writing belongs on the rule at the bottom of the box, centred over the printed name.
findings.where: 1701-2018 p1c125-i, .fh52 = font-size 9pt / line-height 33.24pt in a 34.20pt strip, so the caret sits at mid-height; no text-align is emitted for plain fields, so the UA default (left) applies. Same shape wherever a 'Signature over Printed Name...' caption binds the ruled box above it, including the inputs F211 will add to 0619E/0619F.
findings.evidence: User visual review 2026-08-11: typed into 1701 p1c125 and asked for bottom-aligned, centred text. Split out of F154, whose claim (the input should not exist) is refuted -- this is styling, not correctness, hence minor. Mechanism available without new CSS: the input's inline `inset` already varies per cell (emit.py:2702-2705, computed in field_box emit.py:1478-1569), and the referee's inline-style scan (comb_referee.py:928-948, 3446-3465) does not ban text-align, while the stylesheet allowlist (comb_referee.py:3607-3648) would reject a new CSS class.
findings.resolution: FIXED in T5d by binding a signature strip to the caption below it, the BureauReservation precedent reversed. emit.py gains SignatureLineBinding: for each text run whose (normalised) text contains both 'signature' and 'printed name' -- BIR's own words for 'this is where you sign', in either order the corpus sets them ('Signature over/and Printed Name...' on most, 'Printed Name and Signature...' on 1700/1701/1701A/1701MS/2550-DS plus 2200S's two officer lines) -- the box directly above the run's own owning cell (shared wall, exact 0.0pt gap in every real case) is bound, but ONLY when that box is already kind=field or one of F211's new signature-box claims; an unconstrained adjacency test binds the wrong cell on 2316, whose caption sits below an unrelated 'Date Signed' sub-row with the real signature box two rows further up, so this constraint is load-bearing, not decoration. FieldPlan then re-seats every bound box's writing surface (seat_signature_line) to a single-line strip at the CELL's own bottom -- only the TOP inset grows, by the difference between the box's full height and one natural line at the fitted face -- and field_input_markup adds an inline text-align:center to the same input, never a new CSS class or a new declaration on an existing selector (the referee's inline-style scan does not ban text-align; its stylesheet allowlist would reject either). Measured: 75 boxes across 43 forms are bound -- the 54 F211 creates (every one also carries this caption below it) plus 21 pre-existing 'field' cells, 1701-2018 p1c125 among them (the strip the user typed their name into and confirmed correct, unchanged in kind, only its own <input>'s inline style moves); 11 of 86 reachable caption runs are refused for the reason above (0605, 1604CF, 2550M, 2551M, 2553 set their signature LINE as a vector rule drawn inside the SAME cell as its own caption, a different shape; 2316's two captions sit below an unrelated sub-row). Verified in a real Chromium page: forms/1701-2018/index.html, p1c125-i reads back computed text-align:center and its own box sits flush with its cell's bottom border (13.4px input height inside a 45.6px cell, bottom edges 0.6px apart -- the border); forms/0619e-2018/index.html and forms/0620-2019/index.html, the same for p1c87-i/p1c88-i; screenshots confirm typed text centred on the line above the printed name in every case. tab_check.py stays 53/53 green. A standing corpus-wide self-test (emit.signature_line_corpus_assertions, run by emit.py --self-test) re-derives the claim set and asserts every bound box is centred and no taller than one line. None of the 75 target cells sit inside a growable band, so the band-runtime JSON needed no matching change. extract.py gains a 'signature-line' self-test check pinning the geometric fact the binding depends on (a caption sitting below the wall the box above it also bounds), against 2551Q page 1's own caption below its 'For Individual:' box; a matching synthetic shape in fixtures/rules.pdf backs it with its own source-level mutation. EXPECTED_HTML_STRUCTURE_SHA256 re-pinned for the 43 slugs T5b+T5d together move (landed as one package: doing them separately would re-pin the same forms twice).

findings.what: The ?debug=fields overlay treats grey decorative tint fragments as printed WALLS, so it reports red 'crosses a printed wall' and blue 'printed box with no input' marks for boxes that are not printed boxes at all. This misdirects review: the user asked why correctly placed inputs were flagged red, and the answer is that the reviewer's instrument is wrong, not the form.
findings.where: emit.py:5025-5066 (visibleRects keeps any rect whose fill differs from what is under it) and emit.py:5120-5149 (boxAt closes a box on those faces). No tone test exists anywhere in FIELD_DEBUG_JS; the `vacant` branch at emit.py:5297-5333 has none either.
findings.evidence: Proven case, 1701-2018 p2 item 3 'Filer's Spouse Type': p2c21-i is reported red with over=4.57pt. The wall responsible is h27, x 432.79-448.03 y 131.78-132.26 at gray 0.8509 role=decorative -- a fragment of the row-band tint running THROUGH the Compensation Earner checkbox, not a rule. Seven blue boxes in the same band come from the same tint fragments (h25 h26 h27 h28) closed against the structural rules h21 and h32. Every tone the overlay needs is already in hand: it stores each rect's fill at emit.py:5034, and the role is one parentNode away on the <g class="layer-structural|decorative|knockout"> group (emit.py:428-434). Note that not all blue is phantom -- the Schedule 1 blues in F210 are real, which is exactly why the category has to become trustworthy rather than be suppressed.
findings.resolution: FIXED in T3+T4 (gate r49). The overlay now classifies rects by tone. Two tests, because there are two questions: `isTintTone` asks whether a STROKE can bound a box and splits at RULE_WALL_TINT_SPLIT_GRAY = 0.70, inside the only genuinely empty interval in the corpus tone census (0.651 -> 0.7489); `isDecorPaint` asks whether a box's INTERIOR is a shading pad, over the wider band (STRUCTURAL_MAX_GRAY, 1). The census refuted this plan's own premise: 0.502 and 0.651 are occupied and are WALLS -- mid-grey checkbox outlines, 100% and 94% short box edges -- so the split the plan first assumed would have erased real checkboxes and hidden F210's entire family. Measured over 53 forms: `over` (red) fell to zero or dropped on every form and rose on none; `vacant` (blue) fell on every form and rose on none, ~2,700 -> 130, and after F210 and the ruled blanks landed, 108. The proven case closed: 1701 p2 p2c21-i went from over=4.57pt against the gray 0.8509 tint fragment h27 to `fits`, and the seven phantom blues in that band are gone. 0619E `over` 6 -> 0 and its twelve centavo-separator pads stopped reporting as forgotten fields. Every claim is proven by running the SHIPPED bytes under node: the split is mutated and required to change a verdict, the paint source is passed both arguments and required to disagree, and the two tone tests are required to DISAGREE about 0.651 so a refactor collapsing them trips first. A defect found while proving it is recorded there too: the vacant probe first read visibleRects' filtered output, which made every one of F210's knockout squares invisible.

findings.what: The tab-walk blames the wrong field. The first input the walk reaches is graded green unconditionally, and the walk starts at the DOM-first input rather than the reading-order-first one -- so when the first-focused field is itself the misplaced one, it is marked GREEN and every correctly-ordered field that should have preceded it is marked red-order. The form still fails overall, so no corpus-level false green exists, but the per-field verdicts and the burned-in page markers point a reviewer at the wrong fields, which is the tool's entire purpose.
findings.where: tab_check.py:347 `running_max = -1` makes the first reached entry satisfy `r >= running_max` always; tab_check.py:183 `INIT_JS` focuses `document.querySelector("input.fi")`, i.e. DOM order, not `expected_order[0]`.
findings.evidence: Read directly at HEAD c10ca99 and confirmed by code trace: with two inputs p2 (DOM first, true rank 1) and p1 (DOM second, true rank 0), the sequence [p2,p1] grades p2 green and p1 red-order -- the inverse of the truth. The self-test cannot catch this by construction: SELF_TEST_HTML only builds an inversion reached AFTER a correctly ordered element, never one where the walk STARTS on the misplaced element. Two further self-test gaps in the same file: the cap-hit path (`terminated_by="cap"`) is never exercised though "never silently truncated" is a central claim, and the self-test browser context omits the `device_scale_factor=2` the corpus run uses.
findings.resolution: FIXED (W4 package) in tab_check.py's compute_verdicts: the running_max sentinel (-1) let the first-reached entry pass unconditionally, which is vacuous the moment the DOM-first field is not the reading-order-first one -- with DOM order [p2 (true rank 1), p1 (true rank 0)] the old code graded p2 green and p1 red-order, the inverse of the truth. The fix special-cases only the first counted entry (seq_num==1): it is graded in_order = (rank == 0) instead of the general r >= running_max rule, and running_max is left at its sentinel when that check fails -- exactly the existing rule for any later red-order entry, so nothing else in the algorithm changes. Every entry after the first is graded by the unmodified rule, and the pre-existing self-test case (p1c1/p1c3 green, p1c2 red-order, a defect reached AFTER a correct entry) is unaffected because it never exercises the first-entry branch. Proved by a NEW fixture (SELF_TEST_HTML_DOM_FIRST) built exactly to F214's own evidence shape -- p2 (row 0, left 100, rank 1) placed before p1 (row 0, left 10, rank 0) in the DOM -- asserting the walk really does reach p2 first (sequence[0] == 'p2-i') and then grading p2-i red-order, p1-i green, with nothing red-skipped: the inverse of what the unfixed code produced. The two other self-test gaps F214 named are also closed: SELF_TEST_HTML_CAP_TRAP gives p1 a keydown listener that preventDefault()s every Tab press (the one honest way terminated_by "cap" can happen -- a merely-unfocusable tabindex="-1" input, tried first, does not do it: Tab simply skips it and the walk still reaches <body> in a bounded number of presses) and gives p2 tabindex="-1" so it could never be reached even if the trap were bypassed; the fixture proves terminated_by=="cap", cap_hit is True, presses==cap (54 for a 2-input page), p1-i is green (reached once, via the walk's own initial programmatic focus()) and p2-i is red-skipped rather than silently dropped, and the report's own ok is False. The self-test browser context now uses device_scale_factor=2, matching main()'s corpus-run context (previously the default DPR, proving nothing about the DPR-2 documents this module actually walks). `python3 tools/formgen/tab_check.py --self-test` passes all three fixtures (26 checks, 0 failures) and the full corpus walk stays 53/53 green with identical per-form counts (green/red-skipped/red-order unchanged on every form -- this fix reorders which field is blamed for an EXISTING defect, it introduces no new red and clears no existing one, since a form failing the walk was already failing before this fix and still fails after it, just with the correct field marked).

findings.what: Verdicts are keyed by DOM id with no uniqueness assertion, so duplicate ids would drop a real field out of grading entirely -- a genuine silent false green rather than a red marker.
findings.where: tab_check.py:271-296 `build_expected` and :331-376 `compute_verdicts`, both plain dicts keyed by id.
findings.evidence: Code trace: `input_meta[id]` is overwritten by the second occurrence and `rank = {id: i ...}` keeps only the last, so two physically distinct inputs collapse to one verdict slot while `totals['total']` (len(expected_order)) still counts both. Latent: no duplicate ids exist in the shipped corpus today (fill_check.py already asserts uniqueness elsewhere), but tab_check itself asserts nothing and would not surface the regression.
findings.resolution: FIXED (W4 package). tab_check.py gains DuplicateInputIdError and build_expected raises it the moment a second input claims an id input_meta already holds, instead of silently overwriting the slot -- so compute_verdicts's own rank = {id: i for i, id in enumerate(expected_order)} is safe by construction (expected_order is now guaranteed duplicate-free before compute_verdicts ever sees it), not by a second uniqueness check repeating the first. walk_form catches the exception and returns the same shape of hard per-form failure walk_form already gives "no .page elements found" (ok: False, a named failure string, zero totals) rather than letting a duplicate silently collapse two fields into one verdict slot. Proved directly: calling build_expected on a synthetic two-cell page where both inputs share id "dup-i" raises DuplicateInputIdError naming the id and the page. Latent on the shipped corpus (no duplicate ids exist today, confirmed by the unchanged 53/53 green corpus walk after this change), which is why no --self-test fixture was added for it -- the guard's value is in failing loudly the day a duplicate is ever introduced, not in the current tree.

That fix landed; the corpus is 53/53 green. A stale 'this failure is expected' note beside a hard gate is how a real regression gets waved off.

findings.what: A checker-of-checkers hole: emit.py's independent re-derivation of the field plan never constructs CheckboxSquareWriting and never passes `checkbox_squares` into field_verdict, so field_verdict's checkbox-square branch is unreachable from that self-check. `ruled_blanks` and `signature_boxes` ARE wired in; only checkbox squares are missing.
findings.where: emit.py:8106-8118 (`field_assertions`); the production call site at emit.py:3280-3282 is correctly wired.
findings.evidence: Confirmed by reading and by running the self-tests. Latent only because the pinned self-test form is 2551Q, which carries zero checkbox squares, and gate.py's check_self_tests passes an --ir override only for lattice and fonts, never for emit. If the checkbox-square branch or its argument passing regressed, this self-check would still report PASS. The corpus-wide checkbox_square_corpus_assertions does run over all 53 IRs but reads the SAME FieldPlan/field_verdict pipeline it is checking, so it cannot detect a false negative in CheckboxSquareWriting's own detection.
findings.resolution: FIXED (W4 package). emit.py's field_assertions -- the independent re-derivation of FieldPlan's own fillable set that `python3 tools/formgen/emit.py --self-test` runs -- built its comparison `fillable` list by calling field_verdict directly with only ruled_blanks and signature_boxes wired in; checkbox_squares, knockout_specify and row_numbers were never constructed or passed, so all three of field_verdict's corresponding branches were unreachable from this self-check. All three are now wired in, built the same way the production FieldPlan constructor already builds them (CheckboxSquareWriting, KnockoutSpecifyWriting and RowNumberWriting, one per page, using the same _min_fillable_line_metrics(ir) the production path uses). Latent for checkbox_squares because the pinned self-test form (2551Q) carries zero; latent for knockout_specify and row_numbers by coincidence, not by having zero claims -- checked directly: 2551Q carries 0 row-number claims but 1 knockout-specify claim (p1c187), which was masked because that same cell is ALSO claimed by ruled_blanks (an underscore rule at the bottom of the same caption), and ruled_blanks is checked first in field_verdict's rule order, so the missing knockout_specify wiring was never exercised even though it would have disagreed with FieldPlan's own answer. Proved the bug was real by reproducing the OLD (unwired) computation against 1701-2018, which has 6 real checkbox squares: FieldPlan's own expected set is 407 cells, the old-style fillable (missing the three plans) is 404 -- a genuine 3-cell mismatch field_assertions would have caught had it ever run against this form instead of 2551Q. `every fillable cell has a typing surface` still passes 128 of 128 on the pinned self-test form after the fix (unchanged, since 2551Q's own answer was masked-correct, not wrong), and the corpus-wide checkbox_square_corpus_assertions / knockout_specify_corpus_assertions / row_number_corpus_assertions -- which read the SAME FieldPlan/field_verdict pipeline and so could never have caught this hole themselves, per F217's own evidence -- are unaffected and still pass (22/23/61 claims respectively, 0 unfilled).

findings.what: Two guard asymmetries in field_verdict's new branches, both latent. (1) The ruled-blank and checkbox-square branches return True without consulting BureauReservation, unlike the signature-box branch which routes through it deliberately. (2) The ruled-blank branch also overrides DecorativeShading without documenting the override or requiring its evidence.
findings.where: emit.py:3046-3051 (ruled-blank and checkbox-square branches) vs the signature-box branch immediately after, and the ordinary field path at emit.py:3075-3076 which does refuse a shaded cell.
findings.evidence: Measured at HEAD: zero of the 58 ruled-blank and 22 checkbox-square claims fall inside a Bureau-reserved rectangle, so (1) is latent. For (2) the override is CORRECT on every live case and that was checked by looking, not assumed: of 48 underscore-origin rules sitting on a tint, 41 lie inside a white knockout the sheet paints to clear a writing space, and the 7 without one were rendered and read -- 1801 p1c201 is '...to be paid on or before ____' (a date blank with a visible white box) and 2200A p3c96/c103/c110 and 2200P p2c376/c390 are 'Others (specify)' ATC write-on lines. So an explicitly drawn writing line does beat a background tint; what is missing is that this precedence is nowhere stated and nowhere asserted, so it holds by corpus accident rather than by construction.
findings.resolution: FIXED (W4 package), both halves. (1) field_verdict's ruled-blank and checkbox-square branches now route through BureauReservation exactly as the signature-box branch beside them already does deliberately: `return False, "bureau"` if the claim falls inside a Bureau-reserved rectangle, `return True, "ruled-blank"`/`"checkbox-square"` otherwise. Zero of the corpus's 58 ruled-blank and 22 checkbox-square claims fall inside a Bureau-reserved rectangle today (measured, unchanged after the fix -- the guard was latent, not live), but the asymmetry is closed by construction rather than left to that measurement holding forever. (2) The ruled-blank branch's own DecorativeShading override -- deliberately NOT consulting shading, unlike the ordinary field path a few lines below -- is now documented at the branch itself (previously undocumented, per F218's own finding) and captured by a new standing assertion in ruled_blank_corpus_assertions: among the corpus's 58 ruled-blank claims, 27 sit on shaded paper, and every one of the 27 still has a typing surface (0 lost to shading), asserted in the direction opposite row_number_corpus_assertions's own shaded check (a row number on shaded paper must NOT have an input; a ruled blank on shaded paper must STILL have one), so the override cannot rot into a silent loss the day someone "fixes" it back to consulting shading. The override itself is left exactly as F218 measured it correct: of 48 underscore rules on tint, 41 sit inside a white knockout and the 7 without one are genuine write-on lines (1801 item 21's date blank, 2200A/2200P's "Others (specify)" ATC lines). `python3 tools/formgen/emit.py --self-test` passes with the new assertion (27 shaded ruled-blank claims, 0 without a typing surface) alongside the unmoved checkbox-square/signature-box/knockout-specify/row-number corpus checks.

findings.what: SignatureLineBinding's inline `text-align:center` is applied at static pre-render time but is not mirrored into the growable-band runtime blob, so a signature line inside a band would render centred in the pre-rendered row and left-aligned in every runtime-cloned row.
findings.where: emit.py:3536-3553 `field_json` and emit.py:5312-5324 `fieldMetrics` in BAND_JS emit inset/size/line-height/letter-spacing but never text-align; FieldPlan.centered is read only by field_input_markup at emit.py:3517-3518.
findings.evidence: Measured: zero of the 75 SignatureLineBinding claims (and zero ruled-blank, checkbox-square or signature-box claims) currently fall inside a growable band, so this is latent. It will misrender silently the first time a form combines a growable row with a 'Signature over Printed Name' caption.
findings.resolution: FIXED (W4 package), the structural gap closed even though F219 itself records zero live cases. field_json gains a sparse `centered` key -- present only where `fields.centered` (F212's own set) already holds the cell id, mirroring `region_insets`'s identical sparse shape -- and its one call site (cell_json, which every growable band's band_json blob goes through per row) now passes the cell id it already has. BAND_JS's fieldMetrics gains a fourth parameter, slotIndex, and sets `el.style.textAlign` to "center" when `field.centered` is true AND slotIndex is null -- the identical guard field_input_markup's own inline `text-align:center` already uses (a comb slot never reaches this branch there, and never should here either, even though no comb slot in the corpus currently carries field.centered true). Both call sites of fieldMetrics (fieldInput, for JS-built rows; applyFields, for template-cloned rows) now pass their own already-known slotIndex through. Proved by two synthetic FieldPlan checks in emit.py's own self-test: an uncentred field's band JSON carries no `centered` key at all (matching `region_insets`'s own absence convention), and a field with its id added directly to `FieldPlan.centered` (bypassing SignatureLineBinding's caption detection, which is a separate, already-proven mechanism) does carry `centered: true`; a third check greps the shipped BAND_JS text for `field.centered` and `textAlign` so the mechanism cannot be silently reverted. Measured zero live impact as F219 itself predicted: the band-data JSON blob (`<script type="application/json" id="formgen-bands">`) is byte-identical across all 53 forms before and after this change -- no growable band in this corpus currently combines with a centred field -- so this is a structural fix with no corpus-wide measurement to report, exactly as F219 stated.

findings.what: 99 of the 108 remaining blue 'printed box with no input' marks are phantoms: the overlay closes boxes on vertical faces that do not span them. They are column-header rows, not missing fields, and they dominate the census a reviewer is meant to scan.
findings.where: 2550m-2007 p2 (59 marks) and 1604cf-2008 p1 (40 marks). The overlay's box discovery is emit.py's FIELD_DEBUG_JS `boxAt` and its face-coverage widening.
findings.evidence: Measured at HEAD. 1604CF is the clean case: cell p1c33 (30.2,253.7 to 582.0,281.0, kind=label, 11 runs) is the remittance table's COLUMN-HEADER row -- 'DATE OF REMITTANCE/MONTH', 'NAME OF BANK/BANK CODE/ROR NO., IF ANY', 'TAXES WITHHELD', 'ADJUSTMENT', 'PENALTIES', 'TOTAL AMOUNT REMITTED'. Its six interior verticals (v97 v109 v131 v152 v169 v184) span y 254.2-271.0 only, stopping 9.6pt short of the cell's bottom rule at 280.6 -- which is why the lattice correctly does NOT cut there. Yet a sampled blue box sits at (73.2, 272.88) 53.8x7.68pt, entirely BELOW where those verticals end, so its left and right faces do not exist. 2550M p2 is the same class: its topmost horizontal rule is h0 at y117.8-118.8 and the lattice's first y line is 118.32, so the entire column-header region above it ('Industries Covered by VAT', 'A T C', 'Amount of Sales/Receipts', 'Output Tax', 'For the Period') is unsegmented, and the empty strips between those captions and h0 read as vacant boxes. Neither is explained by the glyph-height floor (4.68pt / 3.58pt); the rows are 7.7-8.6pt tall.
findings.resolution: FIXED (W4 package). FIELD_DEBUG_JS's boxAt/wallsOf gained a new function, crossesCleanly, and a `strict` parameter threading it through wallsOf's L and R (never T/B) member-selection branches. The bug, confirmed by direct measurement in a real Chromium page rather than re-derived from the finding's prose alone: 1604cf-2008 p1c33's phantom at (73.2,272.88)-(127.0,280.56) closes on two REAL, fully-covering vertical rules (the data table's own column dividers) whose ink starts EXACTLY at the box's own T (0.00pt off, because that is the same rule that also defines T) and runs 108.96pt further down through the real rows beneath -- flush on one end, running far past the other, the signature of a rule that belongs to a taller structure and merely grazes this box. crossesCleanly rejects a member with exactly this shape: reaching both ends of the box (a partial-coverage member is untouched) but flush (within TOL, or within TOL of the box's own span for the near side and clearly beyond it on the far side -- the margin is Math.max(TOL, box span), not a fixed point value, because a fixed TOL over-fired: comb ticks routinely overshoot their own writing band by a few tenths of a point on one side only, and a fixed 0.25pt margin called that asymmetric too, costing 9,421 real inputs their box corpus-wide on the first attempt (measured, reverted before landing). Restricted to L/R only: applying the identical check to T/B rejected every EDGE compartment of every comb in the corpus (a comb's shared rail is, by design, flush with its own edge compartment on one side and not the other -- measured, also reverted before landing). Restricted to `strict` mode, applied only from allBoxes' own candidate search (used to build the VACANT population) and never from pageCensus's per-input lookup (which classifies a real input's own fits/small/over/unboxed verdict) -- and this split is provably safe rather than merely careful: any box a real input resolves to is re-added to the candidate set from that non-strict lookup regardless of what allBoxes found, so strict mode can only ever narrow the VACANT population, by construction. Measured before/after on the tree this package actually wrote (all 53 forms regenerated with the fix, `build/html/*.html`): corpus-wide vacant 110 -> 7 (1604cf-2008 p1 40->1, 2550m-2007 p2 59->3, plus five other forms' single stray marks resolving to 0 -- 0619f-2018, 1604c-2018, 1702mx-2018c, 1702q-2018, 1702rt-2018c, 2551m-2002), and fits/small/over/unboxed totals are BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after on every one of the 53 forms (43,731/604/27/240), proving zero real input was reclassified. The 99-of-108-phantom hypothesis from the finding's two named forms was independently validated at full precision before the fix was written (96 of 99 marks on those two forms reject under a preliminary unscaled version of the rule; 3 do not and are exactly the 3 that survive as real in the final shipped rule on 2550m-2007), and the corpus's remaining 7 marks were spot-checked against build/layout: 1604cf-2008's one surviving mark sits inside p1c251, a genuine `label` cell no field-promotion rule claims -- a real "printed box with no input" candidate this package does not resolve (out of scope: no field decision may move) and correctly does not vanish. HTML_RUNTIME_SCRIPT_SHA256 and EXPECTED_HTML_STRUCTURE_SHA256 (comb_referee.py) are re-pinned for both this fix and F219's BAND_JS change together (see that file's own comment for the full byte-identity proof: 53/53 forms identical outside every <script> tag, including the band-data JSON blob). comb_referee's own comb census is unmoved: combs_expected 4587, combs_unevaluable 33, subjects_active 4554, identical before and after. Determinism verified: two independent regenerations of all 53 forms from the fixed emit.py produce byte-identical HTML.

findings.what: Twelve more signature areas cannot be signed -- the same defect as F211 on six forms T5b did not reach. Every one has a printed 'Signature over Printed Name...' caption with no input in the box above it.
findings.evidence: Measured at HEAD by walking every 'Signature over Printed Name' caption run in the IR and testing the cell directly above it for an input in the shipped HTML. Two distinct mechanisms, both disclosed by T5d's agent as deliberate refusals but never filed: on 0605/1604CF/2550M/2551M/2553 the signature LINE is drawn as a vector rule inside the same cell as the caption, so SignatureLineBinding's box-above test finds no separate box to bind; on 2316 the caption binds nothing because an unrelated 'Date Signed' sub-row intervenes between the caption and the real box, and an unconstrained adjacency test was rejected precisely because it bound the wrong cell there.
findings.resolution: MEASURED in W1 (F206): the GEOMETRIC half of F206's knockout-over-tint marker reaches 6 of these 12 areas -- 0605-1999 p1c176, 1604cf-2008 p1c316, 2550m-2007 p1c181, 2551m-2002 p1c175, 2553-1999 p1c216, 2316-2021 p1c337 -- measured directly with emit.knockout_specify_band, its caption gate bypassed: each reports a band 29x to 52x its own form's line width, so these ARE the same tint/knockout tri-partition shape 1801-2018 p2c261 and p1c197 are. 2316-2021 p1c328 and p1c339 return no band at all and p1c326 is kind=blank, not label. But W1's shipped mechanism additionally gates on a caption containing "specify" -- every caption here is "I declare, under the penalties of perjury..." or "Date Signed", never "specify" -- so W1 does NOT reach any of these 12 and leaves them all refused, correctly: a signature area needs the bottom-seated, centred treatment SignatureLineBinding already gives F212's population, not a generic left-anchored text box, and W1 was told not to improvise a second mechanism. Left for W4 with this measurement.

findings.what: Sixteen comb-slot inputs on one cell are reported as crossing a printed wall. Either the slot geometry genuinely overruns its compartments, or the overlay over-reports the wall -- this has never been investigated and the two have opposite fixes.
findings.where: 1701q-2018 p2, comb cell p2c115 (355.61,748.60 to 476.26,769.46, kind=field, border_count=4), slots p2c115-s*.
findings.evidence: The 26 residual overlay reds at HEAD are 1701Q x16, 2550M x5, 2553 x2, 1801 x2, 2551M x1. T3+T4 reduced 1701Q from 30 to 16 by removing tint-fragment phantoms and recorded the remainder as 'pre-existing, real wall-crossing geometry, not investigated'. Note the overlay's own documented bias runs toward over-reporting walls (a rect only PARTLY over a different colour is kept, which can only shrink a box), and F220 now shows boxAt closes boxes on faces that do not span them -- so the over-report hypothesis has to be excluded before any producer change is made.

findings.what: A rule clipped at a page or guide split keeps its pre-split `length_pt` while its coordinates are correctly clipped -- the stale-length inconsistency guides.py's own clip_rule docstring warns about ('a clipped rule that keeps the original length is exactly the false mismatch this pipeline must not manufacture').
findings.where: emit.py:4166-4189 `PageSplit.clipped()` copies only x0/y0/x1/y1 from the clipped piece into `dict(item)`; guides.py:642-654 computes a correct clipped length_pt that is discarded.
findings.evidence: Pre-existing, not introduced by this PR. No consumer of `rule['length_pt']` was found downstream of the merge, so it is currently an unread field -- an inconsistency in the record rather than a live defect.

findings.what: W1's new KnockoutSpecifyWriting mechanism ships with no SOURCE-LEVEL mutation proving its check can fail. The house rule is that every new check gets one, and T5a set the precedent for exactly this situation: when no pinned PDF carried a qualifying cell it added a synthetic shape to fixtures/rules.pdf via make_fixtures.py and a real `checkbox-square` mutation beside it.
findings.where: tools/formgen/fixtures/prove_fixtures_fail.py -- still 19 source-level mutations after W1, unchanged from before it. The mechanism's own proof lives only in emit.py's self-test as `knockout_specify_writing_assertions` (5 paired positive/negative assertions).
findings.evidence: Measured after the W1 merge: `prove-fixtures-fail: PASS over 19 source-level mutations, 6 checks stated as contract-only` -- the same 19 as before W1. The implementing agent disclosed the refusal and its reason (none of extract.py's 7 pinned PDFs contains a cell the mechanism claims, so there is no real-world fact to pin), which is accurate but is the same situation T5a solved by extending the synthetic fixture rather than by declining. Nothing was parked in CONTRACT_ONLY, so this is a missing proof rather than a dodged one; the in-module paired assertions do exercise both directions. Recorded so the erosion is tracked instead of waved through.

findings.what: An implementing agent downgraded the MACHINE-GLOBAL pip `playwright` package from 1.59.0 to 1.58.0 -- outside its own worktree, on a shared environment, against the version CI pins -- on a wrong diagnosis.
findings.where: Machine-global site-packages; CI pins PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION 1.59.0 at .github/workflows/formgen.yml:62.
findings.evidence: The agent reported 1.59.0 was 'blocking tab_check.py entirely' and downgraded to match the cached chromium-1208. That diagnosis is refuted by direct evidence: I ran the full 53-form tab-walk successfully many times on 1.59.0 earlier the same day, and after the downgrade `chromium.launch()` printed the install-browsers banner -- i.e. 1.58.0 does NOT match chromium-1208 and the downgrade broke what it claimed to fix. Beyond the breakage it also diverged the local environment from CI and from audit.py's runtime attestation, which SHA-256 snapshots the entire Playwright package tree.
findings.resolution: FIXED by the operator immediately: reinstalled playwright==1.59.0 and verified `chromium.launch()` returns version 147.0.7727.15 with no banner. No repo bytes were involved. Recorded because the lesson is a process one -- an agent's brief scopes it to a worktree, and machine-global mutation is outside that scope even when it looks like a fix; it also shows an agent's environment diagnosis needs the same measurement discipline as its code claims.
